recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindKotlinAndroidSyntheticImports$KtRecipe
recipes.description: The Kotlin Android Extensions synthetic-view plugin was deprecated in 1.4.20 and removed entirely in later AGP versions. Migrate the call sites to ViewBinding. Each reference here corresponds to a usage that won't compile without the (removed) plugin.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindLifecycleObserveLiveData$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Inside a `Fragment`, `liveData.observe(this, observer)` ties the subscription to the fragment's lifecycle — which outlives the view across `onDestroyView`/`onCreateView` recreation and produces dangling references to a destroyed view. Use `viewLifecycleOwner` instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindLiveDataPostValueFromMain$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `MutableLiveData.postValue(...)` calls inside coroutine main-thread contexts
recipes.description: `postValue` exists for background-thread updaters — it marshals through the main looper and coalesces consecutive updates. When called from a place that already runs on the main thread (UI callbacks, view-model initialization, `Dispatchers.Main` blocks), the coalescing is a footgun: intermediate values silently drop. Use `setValue`/`.value =` on the main thread, `postValue` only from background threads.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindLocalBroadcastManager$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `LocalBroadcastManager` was deprecated in AndroidX 1.1 — the project effectively documents it as a global event bus, with all the ordering and lifetime trouble that implies. Migrate to `LiveData`, `StateFlow`, or `SharedFlow` for in-process pub/sub.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindManualDaggerProvision$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Calls of the form `DaggerXComponent.builder().build()` indicate the application is composing its dependency graph by hand. Hilt (`@HiltAndroidApp` / `@AndroidEntryPoint`) generates the same graph automatically and integrates with Compose, ViewModel, and WorkManager out of the box.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindManualThreadingInActivity$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Hand-rolled `Thread { … }.start()` inside a UI component leaks across configuration changes (the thread outlives the activity) and has no story for cancellation. Migrate to `lifecycleScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO) { … }` or `viewModelScope.launch { … }` — both cancel when the lifecycle ends.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindModeWorldReadable$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Both constants were deprecated in API 17 — they grant any app on the device read or write access to the file. Use a `FileProvider` to share content URIs, or scope the file via `Context.getFilesDir()` and expose it through your own content provider with explicit permissions.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindMutableLiveDataAllocation$KtRecipe
recipes.description: In Kotlin Android code, `MutableStateFlow<T>` is the modern equivalent. It integrates with structured concurrency, exposes the current value synchronously, and composes cleanly with Compose's `collectAsState`/`collectAsStateWithLifecycle`. Each `MutableLiveData()` here is a candidate for migration.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindObjectAnimator$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Direct `ObjectAnimator` use is a candidate for review — for Compose UIs the idiomatic replacement is `animate*AsState` / `Animatable`, which integrate with recomposition and cancellation. For view-system code, `SpringAnimation`/`PhysicsAnimation` cover more interaction shapes than the time-based `ObjectAnimator`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindOnActivityResultOverride$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Every override of `Activity.onActivityResult` / `Fragment.onActivityResult` is half of the deprecated `startActivityForResult` pair. The new Activity Result APIs (`registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.X) { … }`) deliver results to a lambda colocated with the launcher — the override goes away.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindOnRequestPermissionsResultOverride$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Override of `Activity.onRequestPermissionsResult` / `Fragment.onRequestPermissionsResult` — the result-callback half of the deprecated `requestPermissions(...)` pair. Replace with a `registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission)` lambda.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindParcelableJavaImpl$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Manual `writeToParcel` / `CREATOR` implementations are pure boilerplate that the `kotlin-parcelize` plugin generates for any class annotated `@Parcelize`. Each manual implementation is a candidate for migration to the annotation.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindPreferenceManagerGetDefaultSharedPreferences$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `android.preference.*` (framework) was deprecated in API 29. AndroidX `androidx.preference.*` is the supported path, and even there the modern shape for KV state is Jetpack DataStore (`Preferences DataStore` for key/value, `Proto DataStore` for typed records) — which works in `suspend` contexts and survives process death without main-thread blocking.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindPreferenceManagerImport$KtRecipe
recipes.description: The framework `android.preference.*` package was deprecated in API 29. Move to `androidx.preference.*` (drop-in replacement) or, for KV state, Jetpack DataStore — which composes with coroutines and `Flow` instead of running on the main thread.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindPublicMutableLiveDataProperty$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Exposing `MutableLiveData<T>` (or `MutableStateFlow<T>`) to observers lets them mutate the model from the consumer side. The convention is to keep the mutable handle `private` and expose a read-only `LiveData<T>` / `StateFlow<T>` getter, so the owner is the only one that can publish updates.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindRealmUsage$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Realm Java/Kotlin is in maintenance and was effectively superseded by Realm Kotlin (`io.realm.kotlin`) and ultimately by MongoDB Atlas Device SDKs. Each `Realm.getDefaultInstance()` is a candidate for migration to Room + DataStore, or to the modern Realm Kotlin SDK.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindRequestPermissions$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Calling `requestPermissions(...)` directly couples the request to a screen and a request code that has to be matched in `onRequestPermissionsResult`. The modern shape is `registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission()) { granted -> … }` — the result lands in a lambda next to the launcher.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindResourcesGetColor$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Resources.getColor(int)` was deprecated in API 23 — it doesn't take a theme. Replace with `ContextCompat.getColor(context, id)`, which threads the theme through and respects `?attr` references.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindResourcesGetDrawable$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Resources.getDrawable(int)` was deprecated in API 22 — it doesn't take a theme. Replace with `ResourcesCompat.getDrawable(resources, id, theme)` to render themed drawables consistently across API levels.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindRoomQueryWithoutLiveDataOrFlow$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `@Query` DAO methods returning a synchronous result
recipes.description: A non-suspend `@Query` returning `List<X>`, `X?`, or a scalar runs the DB query on the calling thread — by default Room throws `IllegalStateException` if that's the main thread. Mark the function `suspend` (single-shot) or return `Flow<...>` / `LiveData<...>` (observable) so Room can dispatch the query off the main thread.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindRunOnUiThread$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Hand-rolled main-thread dispatch (`runOnUiThread`, `view.post`) was the pre-coroutine pattern for crossing thread boundaries from a background worker. In Kotlin, prefer `withContext(Dispatchers.Main) { … }` — it composes with structured cancellation and surfaces in the call site's coroutine context.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindRuntimeExecInAndroid$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Forking a process from an Android app is almost never the right shape — the system imposes strict app-sandbox limits (no `su`, no arbitrary binaries) and process lifetime is unrelated to the activity that spawned it. Audit each call site against `WorkManager`, foreground services, or — if you genuinely need shell tools — `java.lang.ProcessBuilder` with explicit lifecycle management.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindRxJavaImports$KtRecipe
recipes.description: RxJava is in maintenance and Kotlin's idiomatic story is coroutines + `Flow`. Each import is a candidate for migration to `kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*` (or, at the boundary, `kotlinx-coroutines-rx3`/`kotlinx-coroutines-rx2` adapters during incremental migration).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindSerializableUsage$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.io.Serializable` is reflection-based and slow on Android — it allocates substantially more than `Parcelable` and pulls in field-by-field reflection at deserialize time. For inter-component transport, prefer `@Parcelize` (`kotlin-parcelize`) or `kotlinx.serialization`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindSharedPreferencesCommit$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `commit()` writes to disk on the calling thread (often the main thread, where it can drop a frame). `apply()` writes asynchronously and atomically, returning immediately — use it unless you specifically need the boolean result on the spot.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindSharedPreferencesEdit$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Raw `edit()` calls predate AndroidX `SharedPreferences.edit { … }`, the Kotlin extension that handles `apply`/`commit` for the caller. Replace each `prefs.edit().put*(...).apply()` chain with `prefs.edit { put*(...) }` — same disk write, less ceremony, and harder to drop the apply by accident.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindStartActivityForResult$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `startActivityForResult` was deprecated in AndroidX Activity 1.2 / Fragment 1.3 in favor of the Activity Result APIs (`registerForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.X) { result -> … }`). The new API survives process death, decouples the launcher from the lifecycle owner, and removes the per-screen `onActivityResult` switch.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindStartService$KtRecipe
recipes.description: On API 26+ background apps cannot call `startService(...)` — the system throws `IllegalStateException`. For services that must run while the app is backgrounded, call `ContextCompat.startForegroundService(context, intent)` and post a notification within five seconds. For one-shot work, use `WorkManager` instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindSystemOutInAndroid$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `System.out` on Android writes to logcat under a default tag that's easy to lose. Use `Log.d`/`Log.i` for tagged output (or, better, Timber) — both route through Android's logging pipeline with filterable tags.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindVibratorVibrateLong$KtRecipe
recipes.description: The single-`long` `Vibrator.vibrate(ms)` was deprecated in API 26. Use `Vibrator.vibrate(VibrationEffect.createOneShot(...))` (or `VibratorManager` on API 31+) — both let the platform pick the appropriate amplitude.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindWebViewJavaScriptEnabled$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Enabling JavaScript in a WebView lets the loaded page run arbitrary script in your app's context. For first-party content this is often fine; for any third-party content it's a critical security boundary. Each match is worth reviewing alongside the trust model of the loaded URLs.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.android.FindWebViewLoadUrl$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `WebView.loadUrl(...)` is worth a security review: arbitrary http://-scheme URLs bypass the system browser and inherit the WebView's privileges (cookies, JS bridges). For untrusted content prefer `CustomTabsIntent` (Chrome Custom Tabs) — better security, better UX, no JS bridge.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.BestPractices$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Opinionated bundle of every best-practice recipe in this module: collection / string round-trip collapses, stdlib accessor swaps, and a broad set of search-only flags covering class structure, function declarations, string construction, Boolean conditionals, lambdas, and exception handling. For diff-only output, use `ImproveKotlinBestPractices` instead.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseStdlibAccessors$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Use stdlib accessors for size / first

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.CollapseRedundantConversions$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Drops needless `toList()`/`toMutableList()`/`toSet()`/`toTypedArray()` round-trips and `trimStart().trimEnd()`-style chains that allocate one or more intermediate copies. The replacement performs the same conversion in one pass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindAbstractClassWithoutMembers$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `abstract class` declarations without abstract members
recipes.description: An `abstract class` with no abstract members and no state offers nothing over `interface` — and `interface` composes better (multiple inheritance, no constructor coupling). If the class is being used as a marker, consider `sealed interface` for stronger exhaustiveness checks.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindAlsoPrintln$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `.also { println(it) }` is a side-channel print left over from debugging. It survives compilation, runs in production, and is invisible at the call site — remove it or route the value through a logger.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindAlsoWithEmptyBody$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `x.also { }` calls with an empty body
recipes.description: `x.also { }` with an empty block is a no-op that returns `x`. Drop the call — it adds an allocation for the captured lambda and obscures the value flow.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindAnonymousObjectSingleMethod$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find anonymous `object : Interface { override fun … }` with a single override
recipes.description: An anonymous object that implements one interface with a single function override is the canonical SAM-conversion target. If the interface is declared `fun interface I { … }`, the call site collapses to a lambda.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindBareExceptionThrow$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Throwing bare `Exception` (or `RuntimeException`) loses information that a more specific type would carry. Prefer `IllegalArgumentException` (bad input), `IllegalStateException` (object in wrong state), or a domain-specific subclass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindBareRuntimeExceptionThrow$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Same family as `throw Exception("...")` — flag for replacement with `IllegalArgumentException`/`IllegalStateException`/domain-specific subclass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindBestPracticeCandidates$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Search-only bundle: flags places where a more idiomatic Kotlin spelling is available. Each match shows up as a `SearchResult` for review; nothing is rewritten automatically because the migration is a judgment call.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindAnonymousObjectSingleMethod$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find anonymous `object : Interface { override fun … }` with a single override

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindDoubleBangChain$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find chained `!!` assertions in a single expression

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindBooleanConditionalSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `if (x) true else false`, its inverse, `!x.isEmpty()` / `!x.isBlank()` family negations, `if (x == null) null else x.foo()`, `if (x != null) x.foo()` patterns, and `if (return …) else …` early-return ladders — each is the long form of a single Kotlin operator or method.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindIfNullElseExpression$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `if (x == null) null else x.foo()` patterns

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindIsNotEmptyOnString$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `x.isNotEmpty()` on `String` where `isNotBlank()` might be wanted

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindBooleanLiteralReturnType$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `fun f(): Boolean = true|false` literal-returning functions
recipes.description: A function whose body is literally `true` or `false` is rarely the right shape — either the predicate was a stub left in by mistake, or the value is genuinely constant and should be a `const val`. Either way, surface the call site for human review.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindCatchReturningNull$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Swallowing every exception into `null` discards diagnostic information and conflates 'no value' with 'I lost the cause'. `runCatching { }` returns a `Result<T>` whose `getOrNull()` matches this shape, and `onFailure { }` keeps a hook for diagnostics.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindClassExtendsAny$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Every class implicitly extends `Any` — writing it explicitly only adds noise and a redundant supertype clause.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindClassStructureSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Search-only bundle: flags class-level structural smells (empty companion, empty class body, redundant `: Any()`, manual `toString`/`equals`/`hashCode` trio, named companion of constants, multiple secondary constructors, sealed-class-without-state, marker-object-without-data, empty init, all-val classes that could be `data class`, mutable `data class`/object state, abstract classes without abstract members, and `open` classes with no overridable members).

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindDataObjectCandidates$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find marker `object` declarations that could be `data object`

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindSealedClassWithoutStateCandidates$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `sealed class` declarations that could be `sealed interface`

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindEmptyClassBody$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `class Foo {}` declarations with an empty body

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindMultipleSecondaryConstructors$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find classes with multiple overloaded secondary constructors

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindClassWithoutDataAnnotation$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find classes that could be `data class`

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindAbstractClassWithoutMembers$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `abstract class` declarations without abstract members

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindOpenClassWithoutOverrides$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `open class` declarations without overridable members

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindClassWithoutDataAnnotation$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find classes that could be `data class`
recipes.description: A class whose only members are `val` constructor parameters — no methods, no init, no extra properties — is the canonical shape `data class` exists for. Adding `data` synthesizes `toString`/`equals`/`hashCode`/`copy`/`componentN` without changing any other semantics.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindCompareToInsteadOfOperator$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `x.compareTo(y) > 0` is the long form of `x > y` for any `Comparable<T>` — and `>`/`<`/`>=`/`<=` are defined on `Comparable` to use exactly that call. The operator form reads as the comparison it is, and the bytecode emitted is identical.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindDataClassWithMutableProperty$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `data class` generates `equals` and `hashCode` over the primary-constructor properties. Mutating a `var` property after the instance is stored in a hash-based collection breaks the invariant — the entry can no longer be found by lookup. Prefer `val`; if mutation is needed, model it through `copy(...)`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindDataObjectCandidates$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find marker `object` declarations that could be `data object`
recipes.description: A bare `object Foo` declaration with no body inherits `Any.toString()`, which prints as `Foo$Companion@<hash>`-style identity strings. `data object Foo` (Kotlin 1.9+) generates a readable `toString` (`"Foo"`), `equals` (identity), and `hashCode` — preferred for marker singletons used in `when` exhaustiveness checks and serialization.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindDoubleBangChain$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find chained `!!` assertions in a single expression
recipes.description: `x!!.y!!.z` chains multiple `!!` assertions in one expression. Each one is a separate NPE risk with no diagnostic. Either the intermediate values are non-null (and the assertions can be dropped) or the chain should be modeled with `?.let { }` to surface the absent case explicitly.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindElseAfterReturn$KtRecipe
recipes.description: When the `if` branch returns, the `else` is unreachable as a fall-through guard — the body after the `else` can be moved out of the `else` block, which makes the early-return shape obvious to readers.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindEmptyClassBody$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `class Foo {}` declarations with an empty body
recipes.description: An empty class body `{}` adds no information. Kotlin allows the body to be omitted entirely: `class Foo` is the same declaration without the redundant braces.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindEmptyCompanionObject$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `companion object {}` with no members generates a synthetic `Companion` holder class that's never used. Remove it — Kotlin doesn't require an empty companion object for any feature.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindEmptyInitBlock$KtRecipe
recipes.description: An empty `init {}` block is a no-op. Remove it — every empty initializer is a place a future reader pauses before noticing it does nothing.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindEqualitySmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `===` / `!==` referential checks (usually `==` is meant), `x == true|false` longhand for Boolean, and `x.compareTo(y) > 0` calls that should use the comparison operator directly.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindEqualsToBooleanLiteral$KtRecipe
recipes.description: When `b` is `Boolean`, `b == true` is just `b` and `b == false` is `!b`. The longhand only obscures intent. For `Boolean?` the longhand is meaningful — it returns `false` for `null` rather than failing on `!!` — so leave those alone; flag only the comparison and let the reviewer decide.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindExceptionHandlingSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Throwable.printStackTrace()` (bypasses the logger), bare `throw Exception("…")` / `throw RuntimeException("…")` allocations (lose type information), and `try { } catch (e: Exception) { null }` patterns (collapsible to `runCatching { }.getOrNull()`).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindExplicitUnitReturnType$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find functions with explicit `: Unit` return type
recipes.description: Kotlin functions that don't declare a return type return `Unit` by convention. Writing `: Unit` explicitly adds noise — drop it unless the explicit form aids a generated API surface (e.g. `@JvmOverloads`).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindForceUnwrapInLet$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `x?.let { it!! }` (or `it.foo()!!`) is internally inconsistent: the safe-call entry already guards null, so the `!!` on `it` can never trigger. Drop the `!!` — the lambda body has a non-null receiver by construction.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindForEachAddCandidate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `xs.forEach { ys.add(it) }` is the loop-form of `ys.addAll(xs)`. The bulk operation is a single method call and uses the most efficient copy strategy the receiver supports.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindForEachPrintln$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `forEach { println(it) }` is the loop-form `for (x in xs) println(x)` — verify whether the print is debug-only. If it is intended output, consider `joinToString("\n").let(::println)` to write the whole thing in one syscall.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindFunctionDeclarationSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Search-only bundle: explicit `: Unit` / `: Nothing` return type, block bodies that are a single `return expr`, literal-Boolean-returning functions, `Pair`/`Triple` returns that could be data classes, default-before-required parameters, `suspend fun` declarations returning `Job`/`Deferred`, and explicit `return Unit` statements.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindExplicitUnitReturnType$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find functions with explicit `: Unit` return type

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindReturnTypeNothing$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find functions declared with `: Nothing` return type

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindSingleExpressionBodyCandidate$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `fun foo(): T { return x }` block bodies

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindBooleanLiteralReturnType$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `fun f(): Boolean = true|false` literal-returning functions

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindFunctionReturningPair$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A function returning `Pair<A, B>` forces every caller to remember which side is which. A small `data class Result(val a: A, val b: B)` documents the role of each component and gains `componentN()` / `copy()` for free.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindFunctionReturningTriple$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Same shape as the `Pair` case but the readability cost compounds — three positional components is the limit where most readers stop guessing which is which. Replace with a `data class`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindIfNullElseExpression$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `if (x == null) null else x.foo()` patterns
recipes.description: An `if (x == null) null else x.foo()` collapses to the safe-call `x?.foo()`. The safe-call is structurally null-aware — the longhand re-checks for null without surfacing the absent case in the type system.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindIfReturnFalseElseTrue$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `if (x) false else true` is just `!x`. Replace the inverted Boolean conditional with the negation it already expresses.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindIfReturnTrueElseFalse$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `if (x) true else false` is just `x` after Boolean simplification. The longhand only hides intent.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindIsNotEmptyOnString$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `x.isNotEmpty()` on `String` where `isNotBlank()` might be wanted
recipes.description: `String.isNotEmpty()` returns true for whitespace-only strings. When the check exists to guard against missing user input, `isNotBlank()` is usually closer to the intent.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindLambdaSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Redundant `map { it.toString() }` / `forEach { it.toString() }`, debug-leftover `.also { println(it) }` / `forEach { println(it) }`, `xs.toList().forEach { }` over already-iterable receivers, `.also { it.add(...) }`-built mutable collections, and `forEach { ys.add(it) }` (use `addAll`).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindLazyWithoutMode$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `lazy { }` defaults to `LazyThreadSafetyMode.SYNCHRONIZED` — every read passes a synchronized check. For thread-confined state (UI, single-threaded actors), `lazy(LazyThreadSafetyMode.NONE) { }` avoids the synchronization entirely.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindLetForNotNullCheck$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `if (x != null) { x.foo() }` is the long form of `x?.let { it.foo() }` — or, when only one call is needed and `x` is a local, `x?.foo()`. The safe-call form makes the null-aware path part of the type system rather than a separate Boolean check.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindManualToStringEqualsHashCode$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A class that overrides all three of `toString`, `equals`, and `hashCode` over its own fields is the canonical shape `data class` exists for. Migrate to `data class C(val a: A, …)` to delete the boilerplate and gain `copy()` plus `componentN()` for free.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindMultipleSecondaryConstructors$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find classes with multiple overloaded secondary constructors
recipes.description: Two or more secondary constructors with different arities almost always collapse into a single primary constructor with default arguments. The default-arg form composes with named arguments and `@JvmOverloads` for cross-language interop.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindMutableListAlsoAdd$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Building a list through `mutableListOf<T>().also { it.add(...) }` is the side-channel form of `buildList { add(...) }` (or just `mutableListOf(x)` if every element is known up front). The builder form makes intent explicit.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindMutableMapAlsoPut$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Same shape as `mutableListOf().also { it.add(...) }` for maps. The builder form (`buildMap { put(...) }`) makes the entries visible without the side-channel `it.put`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindMutableSetAlsoAdd$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Same shape as the `mutableListOf` variant — use `buildSet { add(...) }` for the same readability gain.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindNamedCompanionObjectOfConstants$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `companion object Constants { const val X = ... }` adds a named singleton to hold what are essentially file-level constants. Promote the constants to top-level `const val`s — they read the same and avoid the synthetic holder class.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindNegatedIsBlank$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Kotlin's `String.isNotBlank()` is the direct positive form. The negated-blank check reads the same value without the leading `!`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindNegatedIsEmpty$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Kotlin ships `isNotEmpty()` directly on `String`, `Collection`, and `Map`. The negation reads top-down without re-parsing the `!`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindNegatedIsNotBlank$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `!x.isNotBlank()` is the long form of `x.isBlank()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindNegatedIsNotEmpty$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `!x.isNotEmpty()` is the long form of `x.isEmpty()`. Use the direct positive call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindObjectWithMutableState$KtRecipe
recipes.description: An `object` is a singleton — its `var` properties are shared global mutable state. Concurrent reads/writes race without synchronization, and the value can change in surprising ways across modules.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindOpenClassWithoutOverrides$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `open class` declarations without overridable members
recipes.description: The `open` modifier on a class only matters if subclasses override something. A bare `open class Foo` (or one whose members are all `final`) signals an intent — "this class is meant to be extended" — that the type system can't actually enforce. Either declare specific members `open` (and drop the class-level `open`) or remove the modifier entirely.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindRedundantReturnUnit$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Functions that return `Unit` don't need an explicit return at all — `return` (no expression) or simply falling off the end is the conventional shape. Writing `return Unit` repeats the implicit value.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindRedundantToStringInForEach$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `it.toString()` inside a `forEach` evaluates the call but discards the result — equivalent to `forEach {}`. Either the side effect on `toString()` is the goal (very unusual) or the call is dead code.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindRedundantToStringInMap$KtRecipe
recipes.description: If the producer already returns a type whose `toString()` is the desired representation, the `map` is a no-op. If the goal is to materialize the `String`s up-front, `joinToString()` / `toString()` on the collection is usually a better fit.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindReferentialEquality$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Kotlin's `===` checks reference identity, ignoring `equals`. For `data class` and other value-like types this almost always wants `==` instead. Flag every referential check for review — true reference comparisons (e.g. sentinel `Any` objects) are legitimate but rare.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindReturnTypeNothing$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find functions declared with `: Nothing` return type
recipes.description: `Nothing` means 'this function never returns normally' — the body must `throw`, loop forever, or call another `Nothing`-returning function. Flag for review: if the body actually does return, the type is wrong; if it always throws, the call sites can rely on Kotlin's exhaustiveness checks.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindRunWithEmptyBody$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `run { }` calls with an empty body
recipes.description: `run { }` is a scope function for evaluating a block as an expression with an implicit `this` receiver. If the block is empty, the call evaluates to `Unit` and does nothing — drop it.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindScopeFunctionSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `run { }` with empty or no-`this` bodies, `also { }` with empty bodies, and `?.let { … !! }` patterns where the null-guard and force-unwrap contradict each other.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindRunWithEmptyBody$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `run { }` calls with an empty body

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindStandaloneRunWithoutThis$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find top-level `run { … }` whose body never uses `this`

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindAlsoWithEmptyBody$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `x.also { }` calls with an empty body

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindSealedClassWithoutStateCandidates$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `sealed class` declarations that could be `sealed interface`
recipes.description: A `sealed class` with no constructor parameters and no fields adds no expressive power over `sealed interface`. The interface form composes better (allows multiple inheritance, supports `data object` direct implementation, makes the no-state contract explicit).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindSingleExpressionBodyCandidate$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `fun foo(): T { return x }` block bodies
recipes.description: A function whose entire body is a single `return expr` is the canonical shape for Kotlin's single-expression-body syntax (`fun foo(): T = expr`). The expression form makes type inference more useful and removes one level of brace nesting.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindStandaloneRunWithoutThis$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find top-level `run { … }` whose body never uses `this`
recipes.description: Top-level `run { … }` (no receiver) is meaningful only when the block uses the implicit `this` or executes multiple statements as an expression. If the body neither references `this` nor depends on the scoping it provides, the wrapper just adds an unnecessary lambda allocation.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindStringConcatWithEmptyLeft$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prepending an empty `""` is a Java idiom for forcing a `toString()` conversion. In Kotlin write `x.toString()` or the template `"$x"` for the same effect with explicit intent.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindStringConcatWithEmptyRight$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Appending an empty `""` is the inverse of the Java `"" + x` idiom. Use `x.toString()` or `"$x"` instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindStringConstructionSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Trivial `String.format("%s", x)` calls and `"" + x` / `x + ""` concatenations that read more clearly as Kotlin string templates.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindStringFormatTrivial$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `String.format("%s", x)` is the long-hand for the Kotlin string template `"$x"`. The template avoids the per-call format-string parse and reads as the thing it produces.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindSuspendFunctionReturningJob$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `suspend fun foo(): Job` is almost always a confusion of two patterns — either the function should suspend and return a value (drop the `Job`/`Deferred`), or it should launch and return the handle (drop `suspend`, and call `coroutineScope { launch { … } }` internally).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindThrowablePrintStackTrace$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `printStackTrace()` writes the throwable straight to `System.err`, bypassing whatever structured logger the application uses. Route the throwable through a logger so log levels, MDCs, and sinks apply.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindToListBeforeForEach$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Iterable.forEach` already iterates without materializing a list. The intermediate `toList()` allocates a copy that's read once and discarded.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindWhenAsStatement$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `when` used as a statement (its result is discarded) often obscures intent — either the writer expected an expression value or each branch is a side-effecting block that would read more clearly as `if`/`else if`. Flag for review.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindWhenSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `when` expressions that read awkwardly: missing `else`, single-branch, used as statement, with duplicate branch bodies that should collapse to comma-separated labels, or with a Boolean selector that should be `if`.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindWhenWithSingleBranch$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `when (x) { A -> … }` with a single branch

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindWhenWithIdenticalBranches$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `when` with two or more branches having identical bodies

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindWhenWithBooleanSubject$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `when (b) { true -> … false -> … }` is the long form of `if (b) …` — and the `when` reads as if it might gain a third branch, which Boolean cannot. Replace with `if`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindWhenWithIdenticalBranches$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `when` with two or more branches having identical bodies
recipes.description: `when (x) { A -> f(); B -> f() }` repeats the same body for distinct labels — collapse to a single branch with comma-separated labels: `A, B -> f()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindWhenWithoutElse$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `when (x)` used as an expression requires exhaustiveness — without an `else`, the compiler can only prove it for sealed/`enum` selectors. Used as a statement, the missing `else` is a tripwire: any new variant silently falls through. Flag for review.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindWhenWithSingleBranch$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `when (x) { A -> … }` with a single branch
recipes.description: A single-branch `when (x) { A -> … }` is the long form of `if (x == A) …`. The `if` reads more directly and doesn't suggest the branch list will grow.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.FindWildcardImport$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Wildcard imports pull every public symbol from a package — they hide the dependency surface and make incremental compilation more conservative. Prefer explicit per-symbol imports.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.ImproveKotlinBestPractices$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Autofix-only best-practice bundle: collection / string round-trip collapses and stdlib accessor swaps. Excludes the search-only `Find*` recipes so the run output is just diffs, not a flood of search results.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseStdlibAccessors$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Use stdlib accessors for size / first

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseFirstForGetZero$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `first()` reads more naturally than `get(0)` and gives the same compile-time bounds guarantees — both throw `NoSuchElementException`/`IndexOutOfBoundsException` on an empty list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseLengthForCountNoPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `String.count()` walks every character and increments a counter. `length` reads the precomputed size off the `String` header.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseSizeForCountNoPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Collection.count()` without a predicate walks the iterable. `size` reads the precomputed property on `Collection`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseStdlibAccessors$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Use stdlib accessors for size / first
recipes.description: Replaces walk-based accessors with their O(1) property/method equivalents — `count()`/`length`/`size` and `get(0)`/`first()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseToListForToMutableListThenToList$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `toMutableList()` allocates a mutable copy, then `toList()` copies it again to an immutable list. `toList()` directly does what's needed in one pass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseToListForToSetThenToList$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `distinct()` returns a `List` with duplicates removed in one pass. `toSet().toList()` allocates a set and then copies its contents into a list — two allocations to do the same job, and the order semantics differ subtly because hash-based sets don't preserve insertion order across all platforms.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseToSetForDistinctThenToSet$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `toSet()` deduplicates while building the set. `distinct().toSet()` allocates a `List` of distinct elements first, then copies into the set.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseToSetForToListThenToSet$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `toSet()` works on any `Iterable`. The intermediate `toList()` just allocates a list that's immediately discarded.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseToStringForStringToString$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Calling `toString()` on a value that is already a `String` is a no-op that compiles to a method call returning the same reference.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseToTypedArrayForToListThenToTypedArray$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `toTypedArray()` accepts any `Collection`; the intermediate `toList()` just allocates a list that's immediately discarded.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseTrimForTrimEndThenTrimStart$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Same as the inverse — `trim()` strips both ends in one pass without the intermediate `String` allocation.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.bestpractices.UseTrimForTrimStartThenTrimEnd$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `trim()` strips whitespace from both ends in a single pass with no intermediate allocation. `trimStart().trimEnd()` builds a temporary `String` for the left-trimmed value before the second pass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.cleanup.EqualsMethodUsage
recipes.displayName: Structural equality tests should use `==` or `!=`
recipes.description:
In Kotlin, `==` means structural equality and `!=` structural inequality and both map to the left-side term’s `equals()` function. It is, therefore, redundant to call `equals()` as a function. Also, `==` and `!=` are more general than `equals()` and `!equals()` because it allows either of both operands to be `null`.
Developers using `equals()` instead of `==` or `!=` is often the result of adapting styles from other languages like Java, where `==` means reference equality and `!=` means reference inequality.
The `==` and `!=` operators are a more concise and elegant way to test structural equality than calling a function.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.cleanup.ImplicitParameterInLambda
recipes.displayName: `it` shouldn't be used as a lambda parameter name
recipes.description: `it` is a special identifier that allows you to refer to the current parameter being passed to a lambda expression without explicitly naming the parameter. Lambda expressions are a concise way of writing anonymous functions. Many lambda expressions have only one parameter, when this is true the compiler can determine the parameter type by context. Thus when using it with single parameter lambda expressions, you do not need to declare the type.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.cleanup.RemoveLambdaArgumentParentheses
recipes.displayName: Remove method invocation parentheses around single lambda argument
recipes.description: For example, convert `1.let({ it + 1 })` to `1.let { it + 1 }`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.cleanup.RemoveTrailingComma
recipes.description: Remove trailing commas in variable, parameter, and class property lists.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.cleanup.RemoveTrailingSemicolon
recipes.description: Some Java programmers may mistakenly add semicolons at the end when writing Kotlin code, but in reality, they are not necessary.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.cleanup.ReplaceCharToIntWithCode
recipes.description: Replace the usage of the deprecated `Char#toInt()` with `Char#code`. Please ensure that your Kotlin version is 1.5 or later to support the `Char#code` property. Note that the current implementation does not perform a Kotlin version check.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.cleanup.UnnecessaryTypeParentheses
recipes.displayName: Remove unnecessary parentheses on Kotlin types
recipes.description: In Kotlin, it's possible to add redundant nested parentheses in type definitions. This recipe is designed to remove those unnecessary parentheses.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.Compose$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find Compose stability and recomposition issues
recipes.description: Search-only recipes that surface Jetpack Compose anti-patterns the Android docs and Compose stability guide call out: unstable parameter types, mutable classes annotated `@Stable`/`@Immutable`, inline `Modifier` allocations, missing `remember` keys, effect-handler misuse, navigation inside composable bodies, single-child layout wrappers, lazy-list items without keys, and API-shape violations. Each match is a `SearchResult` for human review — Compose remedies are judgement calls (hoist? wrap? annotate? split?) that depend on context outside any one expression. For diff-only output on the small autofix set, use `ImproveKotlinCompose`.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLifecycleAwareFlowSmells$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find lifecycle-naive flow / LiveData collection in Composables

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.UseSpecializedComposeStateContainers$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `remember { mutableStateOf(emptyList/Map()) }` candidates for snapshot-aware containers

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindArrayParameterOnComposable$KtRecipe
recipes.description: JVM arrays are mutable references — Compose's stability inferrer marks an `Array<T>` parameter unstable, forcing the composable to recompose every time the parent recomposes. Prefer `ImmutableList<T>` or a `@Stable` wrapper.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindBoxWithSingleChild$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `Box { OneChild() }` adds a layout node and a measurement pass for no compositional benefit — the child could be invoked directly with the same `Modifier`. Either pull the modifier onto the child or use the explicit `Box` placement APIs if alignment is doing real work.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindByRememberWithoutMutableState$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `by remember { … }` delegations whose body isn't a `mutableStateOf`
recipes.description: `by remember { … }` pairs with a `MutableState<T>` so the property delegates its read/write through the snapshot system. If the `remember { }` body returns a plain `T`, the `by` does nothing useful — and is a strong hint the author forgot to wrap the value in `mutableStateOf(...)` or `derivedStateOf { … }`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindCanvasInComposable$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Canvas { drawXxx(...) }` re-runs the draw lambda on every recomposition; allocating `Paint`, `Path`, or `Brush` instances inside the lambda creates GC pressure that shows up as jank. Review for hoistable allocations (`remember { Paint().apply { … } }`) and for `drawWithCache { … }` opportunities.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindCardWithSingleChild$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `Card { OneChild() }` allocates a layout node and an elevation surface for exactly one composable. If the child already styles itself (`Modifier.background`/`Modifier.shadow`), the `Card` is decorative duplication — pull the styling into the child's `Modifier` chain.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindColumnWithSingleChild$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `Column { OneChild() }` allocates a layout node and runs the column measurement to position exactly one child. Either remove the column or replace with `Box(modifier = m)` if the column's `verticalArrangement` actually does work the parent isn't.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposableCallInNonComposableLambda$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `@Composable` calls inside non-`@Composable` lambda parameters
recipes.description: A `@Composable` function called from inside a non-Composable lambda (e.g., a `forEach { }`) won't enter the composition tree correctly — the function executes but its emitted nodes don't get tracked for invalidation. Either move the call out of the lambda, or use a Compose-aware iterator (`items(list) { … }`).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposableConventionSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Function-naming patterns the Compose API guide calls out: non-`@Composable` functions that use composable APIs (`remember`/`LaunchedEffect`/`rememberCoroutineScope`) without the annotation.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposableLambdaParamMissingDefault$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `@Composable` functions with a content lambda parameter not defaulted to `{}`
recipes.description: By Material/Compose convention, content slot lambdas (`content: @Composable () -> Unit`) default to `{}` so callers can compose the function without supplying a body when they only want the surrounding chrome. Flag content slots without defaults so the API gets the convention-conforming overload.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposableMissingModifierParam$KtRecipe
recipes.description: The Compose API guideline says every composable that emits UI should accept a `Modifier` parameter (named `modifier`, defaulted to `Modifier`) so callers can size, layout, and decorate without subclassing. Flag composables that emit content but expose no `Modifier` slot.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposableWithReturnValue$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `@Composable fun … (): X` functions returning a non-`Unit` value
recipes.description: A `@Composable` function that returns a value either emits UI as a side-effect (anti-pattern: invocation order is now load-bearing) or computes a derived value that should be a `@ReadOnlyComposable`. Mark explicit value-returning composables `@ReadOnlyComposable` so callers know they don't emit, or split into emitting-vs-returning pairs.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposeApiDesignIssues$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Composable functions that don't follow the Compose API guidelines: lowercase name (UI emitters should be `PascalCase`), non-`Unit` return without `@ReadOnlyComposable`, content slot without a default `{}`, missing `Modifier` parameter, and `@Composable` invocations from non-Composable lambdas.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLowercaseComposableFunction$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `@Composable` functions whose name starts with a lowercase letter

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposableWithReturnValue$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `@Composable fun … (): X` functions returning a non-`Unit` value

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposableLambdaParamMissingDefault$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `@Composable` functions with a content lambda parameter not defaulted to `{}`

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposableCallInNonComposableLambda$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `@Composable` calls inside non-`@Composable` lambda parameters

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposeEffectIssues$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Effect handlers misused: `LaunchedEffect(Unit)`/`LaunchedEffect(true)` placeholder keys, `DisposableEffect` lambdas missing `onDispose { }`, `rememberCoroutineScope()` mis-placed inside a lambda, `LaunchedEffect` inside loops, and side-effecting calls (logging, `File`) inside the composable body rather than an effect block.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposeLayoutIssues$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Layout containers that exist for no compositional benefit: `Box`/`Column`/`Row` wrapping a single child, and `LazyColumn`/`LazyRow` items missing a stable `key` (which churns composition state on reorder).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposeModifierIssues$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Modifier-chain shapes that allocate per recomposition (`Modifier.padding(...)` inline), branch with structurally distinct chains (`if (x) Modifier.foo() else Modifier`), or stack `fillMax`/`padding` in a layout-changing order. Each match needs the author's intent to fix correctly.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposeNavigationIssues$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Calls that need to be wrapped in an effect handler or event handler: `navController.navigate(...)` from a composable body, `scope.launch { … }` outside `LaunchedEffect`, lifecycle-naive `collectAsState` instead of `collectAsStateWithLifecycle`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposeRememberIssues$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `remember { … }` calls where the keys do not align with the values the block reads — keyless `remember` that captures changing variables, and `remember { mutableStateOf(call()) }` candidates for `derivedStateOf`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposeStabilityIssues$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Surface declarations where Compose's stability inferrer will refuse to mark a parameter, property, or class as stable: `MutableList`/`MutableMap`/`MutableSet` parameters, read-only `List` parameters, `@Stable`/`@Immutable` annotations applied to classes with `var` fields, and `data class` declarations holding `List<T>` properties.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposeStateReadIssues$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Patterns where a `MutableState`/`State` is read or constructed in a way that loses the snapshot value: explicit `.value` reads, bare `mutableStateOf` without `remember`, class-field state ownership, missing `derivedStateOf`, transient collection allocations.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindMutableStateInClassField$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `mutableStateOf(...)` stored in a class field

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindComposeViewModelIssues$KtRecipe
recipes.description: ViewModel acquisition inside composables — `hiltViewModel<X>()` and `viewModel<X>()` — and StateFlow exposure: `MutableStateFlow` without an `asStateFlow()` read-only view.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindConditionalModifier$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `if (cond) Modifier.foo() else Modifier` returns two structurally different `Modifier` chains, breaking memoization on the consumer. Use `Modifier.then(if (cond) Modifier.foo() else Modifier)` or `Modifier.composed { if (cond) padding(8.dp) else this }` so the consumer sees a single stable reference.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindContextParameterOnComposable$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Passing a `Context` into a composable couples it to the activity instance and makes the function harder to preview/test. Use `LocalContext.current` inside the composable instead — it works through the composition tree and is preview-safe.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindCoroutineLaunchInComposableBody$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `scope.launch { … }` in a `@Composable` body starts a new coroutine on every recomposition — none of them get cancelled until the scope dies. Use `LaunchedEffect(key) { … }`, which is automatically cancelled and restarted by the composition's lifecycle.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindCoroutineLaunchInsideLaunchedEffectInLoop$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `LaunchedEffect` inside a loop creates a separate coroutine per iteration. That is rarely the intended structure — it is usually a mis-placement of effect logic. Prefer a single `LaunchedEffect(keys = arrayOf(...)) { for (...) { … } }` or restructure the loop to live inside the effect.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindDataClassWithListProperty$KtRecipe
recipes.description: When a `data class` is passed to a `@Composable` and one of its properties is a `kotlin.collections.List<T>`, Compose marks the entire class unstable. Wrap the list in `ImmutableList<T>` from `kotlinx.collections.immutable` (or split the list out and remember it separately) so stability inference can prove the holder is `@Stable`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindDerivedStateOfCandidate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `remember { mutableStateOf(expensiveCall()) }` evaluates the expression once and stores it — but if the expression depends on snapshot state, you want it to recompute when that state changes. `derivedStateOf { expensiveCall() }` (inside a `remember { }`) recomputes lazily only when its tracked reads invalidate, instead of either staling out or recomputing on every recomposition.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindDisposableEffectMissingOnDispose$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `DisposableEffect`'s contract is to return a `DisposableEffectResult` from `onDispose { … }` — without it, the compiler should reject the block, but easy mistakes (early `return`, wrong receiver) silently bypass cleanup. Confirm the final statement of every `DisposableEffect` lambda is an `onDispose { }` call so resources are released on leave-the-composition.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindDpAllocationInComposableBody$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Dp` is an inline value class — most `.dp` accesses compile to a primitive. But certain platforms (older Kotlin, KMP non-JVM targets) box the value. In hot composables, prefer hoisting `private val padding = 8.dp` to file scope so the conversion runs once.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindFlowCollectAsState$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `collectAsState()` keeps collecting whenever the composition is alive, including while the host activity is stopped. `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` (from `androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-runtime-compose`) ties collection to the lifecycle owner, dropping subscription while in the background and freeing the upstream `Flow` from doing work nothing will display.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindFlowParameterOnComposable$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Passing a `Flow<T>` into a `@Composable` shifts collection from a `LaunchedEffect` to the consumer — but if the caller re-creates the `Flow` per recomposition, collection restarts every time. Prefer collecting at the call site and passing the resulting `State<T>` (or `T` directly).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindHardcodedColor$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Hardcoded `Color` literals inside a composable bypass `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.X`, breaking light/dark theme adaptation and theming overrides. Move the literal into the theme (a `ColorScheme` extension or a top-level theme val) and read it via `MaterialTheme.colorScheme` at the call site.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindHardcodedDesignTokens$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Color(0xFF…)` literals inside composables break theming and accessibility (light/dark). Hoist into `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.*`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindHiltViewModelInComposable$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `hiltViewModel<MyViewModel>()` inside a `@Composable` couples the screen-level dependency injection to that composable. That is the recommended pattern at navigation entry points, but flagged for review when the same ViewModel is injected from multiple composables (you'll get distinct instances per nav graph entry).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindImmutableAnnotationOnMutableClass$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `@Immutable` is the stronger sibling of `@Stable`: it promises that all public properties are observably unchangeable after construction. A `var` field is by definition observably changeable — Compose will assume it can skip recompositions safely and miss updates. Drop the annotation or convert the property to `val` (and a private backing var if needed).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindInlineModifierConstruction$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `Modifier.padding(...)`-style chain allocates a fresh `Modifier` instance, and a fresh `Modifier` defeats Compose's structural-equality skip — every recomposition allocates again and forces re-layout. Hoist the modifier into a `remember { Modifier… }`, accept a `Modifier` parameter from the caller, or build static modifiers as top-level vals.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLambdaAsComposableParamWithoutNoinline$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Function-typed parameters are unstable from Compose's stability inferrer perspective unless the lambda reference is stable (e.g., function reference or `remember`d). For frequently-recomposed composables, accept a `(T) -> Unit` and document caller responsibility, or fold the callback into a stable holder. Flag for review when the API is performance-sensitive.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLambdaCapturingMutableStateInItems$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find lazy-list `items(...) { … }` content lambdas that read a `MutableState` from the enclosing scope
recipes.description: When a `LazyColumn`/`LazyRow` content lambda reads a `MutableState`/`State` from the enclosing scope, every change to that state invalidates the entire item composition. Hoist the state into a per-item `remember`, or read it inside a child composable so only the affected item recomposes.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLaunchedEffectMultipleSuspendCalls$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `LaunchedEffect` bodies with several distinct suspend calls
recipes.description: A `LaunchedEffect` lambda that issues several distinct top-level suspend calls is usually doing two things: a long-running collector plus an unrelated kickoff. Split them into separate `LaunchedEffect`s keyed independently so canceling one doesn't cancel the other on key changes.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLaunchedEffectWithoutKey$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `LaunchedEffect { … }` calls with no key argument
recipes.description: `LaunchedEffect` always takes at least one key — without one the call is a compile error (or silently rebound to a `(suspend () -> Unit)` overload in stubbed builds). Confirm a key is supplied; `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { … }` is the canonical one-shot spelling.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLaunchedEffectWithTrueKey$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `LaunchedEffect(true)` (or any literal `true`/`false` key) is a one-shot effect dressed up to look like it has a key. It is structurally identical to `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` but reads as if the author meant to pass a variable. Switch to `Unit` for clarity or pass the real dependency.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLaunchedEffectWithUnitKey$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { … }` runs exactly once per composition lifetime — that's intentional for one-shot startup work, but it is also the easiest spelling when the author wanted lifecycle-aware re-launch on a real key. Confirm `Unit` was intentional and not a placeholder for the actual dependencies the effect reads.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLazyColumnDirectCall$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `LazyColumn { … }` calls — verify items use stable keys
recipes.description: A `LazyColumn { items(...) { … } }` whose inner `items` call has no `key = { … }` recomposes every visible row on every reorder/insertion. Audit the call to add a stable key.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLazyListItemMissingKey$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Without a stable `key`, `LazyColumn`/`LazyRow` indexes items by position. Inserting an item shifts every following index and Compose has to recompose every visible child, recreating their state. A stable `key` (typically an id) lets Compose preserve composition state across reorderings and animations.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLazyRowDirectCall$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `LazyRow { … }` calls — verify items use stable keys
recipes.description: A `LazyRow { items(...) { … } }` whose inner `items` call has no `key = { … }` recomposes every visible cell on every reorder. Audit the call to add a stable key.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLazyVerticalGridDirectCall$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `LazyVerticalGrid { … }` calls — verify items use stable keys
recipes.description: A `LazyVerticalGrid { items(...) { … } }` whose inner `items` call has no `key = { … }` recomposes every visible cell on every reorder. Audit the call to add a stable key.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLifecycleAwareFlowSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find lifecycle-naive flow / LiveData collection in Composables
recipes.description: Collectors and observers that keep running while the host activity is stopped: `LiveData.observeAsState()`, `viewModel.uiState.collectAsState()` (vs `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`), and `LiveData.observe(...)` called directly from a `@Composable`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindListAsComposableParam$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `kotlin.collections.List` (and friends) are read-only views, not immutable types — a `List<T>` can be a `MutableList<T>` upcast, so Compose's stability inferrer marks the parameter unstable and re-invokes the composable on every parent recomposition. Use `ImmutableList<T>` from `kotlinx.collections.immutable` or wrap in a `@Immutable` data holder.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindListOfInComposableBody$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `listOf(a, b)` allocates a fresh `List` on every recomposition. If the composable downstream is `@Stable` and compares its inputs by reference, the new list defeats memoization. Hoist into a `remember { listOf(a, b) }` or convert to an `ImmutableList` declared at file scope.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLiveDataObserveInComposable$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `LiveData.observe(lifecycleOwner, observer)` is for `Activity`/`Fragment` code; inside a `@Composable` it registers a brand-new observer on every recomposition and never removes it. Use `observeAsState()` (or migrate to `StateFlow` and `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLongModifierChain$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `Modifier.xxx().yyy()...` chains longer than five operations
recipes.description: A `Modifier` chain with more than five operations is hard to read, hard to memoize, and often hides a hoist-into-a-named-Modifier opportunity. Extract the chain into a `val styled = Modifier…` declaration (ideally `remember`ed at the call site) so the composable body reads as intent rather than plumbing.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLowercaseComposableFunction$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `@Composable` functions whose name starts with a lowercase letter
recipes.description: Compose convention: composables that emit UI use `PascalCase` to set them apart from regular Kotlin functions in IDE auto-complete and stack traces. Lowercase-named composables either should be renamed or, if they return a value rather than emit UI, marked `@ReadOnlyComposable` to signal they don't compose.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierClickableBeforeBackground$KtRecipe
recipes.description: When `clickable` precedes `background` in a `Modifier` chain, the background paints on top of the touch target — the visible color is the background, but the ripple/feedback originates from the layer underneath, which usually isn't the look the author wanted. Place `background(...)` first and `clickable { … }` last so the touch surface sits above the visual fill.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierFillMaxAndPaddingOrderSmell$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Modifier order matters: `Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(8.dp)` fills the parent first and then insets — the visible content is smaller than the parent. `Modifier.padding(8.dp).fillMaxSize()` insets the available space and then fills it, producing a layout that hugs the padded box. The right order is intent-specific; flag chains for review.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierFillMaxWidthAfterFillMaxSize$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `fillMaxSize()` already constrains both width and height — appending `fillMaxWidth()` is redundant and signals the author wasn't sure which size operator they wanted. Drop the second call or swap to the single operator that captures the intent.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierOrderingSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Modifier chains whose order produces a subtly wrong visual or interactive shape: `clickable` painted over by a later `background`, `fillMaxWidth` followed by `padding` (inset *after* the fill), and `fillMaxSize` immediately followed by a redundant `fillMaxWidth`/`fillMaxHeight`. Also surfaces `Modifier.weight(...)` calls outside a `Row`/`Column` scope, and overly long chains that could be hoisted into a named modifier.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLongModifierChain$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `Modifier.xxx().yyy()...` chains longer than five operations

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierPaddingAfterFillMaxWidth$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `fillMaxWidth()` followed by `padding(...)` reserves the full width and then insets — the visible content is narrower than the parent. Most authors who write that chain meant `padding(...).fillMaxWidth()` so the inset comes first and the fill happens inside the inset region. The right order is intent-specific; flag for review.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierPaddingAllEqual$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `padding(start = x, end = x, top = x, bottom = x)` shorthand opportunities
recipes.description: When every named `padding(...)` argument carries the same value, `padding(all = x)` (or just `padding(x)`) communicates the uniform inset in a single token. Mixed-value `padding(...)` is fine; equal-on-all-sides is a shorthand candidate.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierPaddingHorizontalEqualToVertical$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `padding(start = x, end = x, top = y, bottom = y)` shorthand opportunities
recipes.description: `Modifier.padding(start = 8.dp, end = 8.dp, top = 16.dp, bottom = 16.dp)` reads as four independent insets but really means "8 horizontal, 16 vertical". The shorter `padding(horizontal = 8.dp, vertical = 16.dp)` says that intent up front and survives a future change to one axis without re-pairing the values.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierPaddingZero$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Modifier.padding(0.dp)` allocates a `PaddingValues` and a layout pass to inset by zero — the call is a no-op in terms of layout but not at runtime. Drop the call (or split out the surrounding chain so the zero edge isn't expressed at all).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierShorthands$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Named-argument `padding(...)` calls whose values reduce to a shorter spelling: equal start/end + equal top/bottom collapses to `padding(horizontal = x, vertical = y)`; all-equal collapses to `padding(all = x)`; all-zero is a removable no-op.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierPaddingHorizontalEqualToVertical$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `padding(start = x, end = x, top = y, bottom = y)` shorthand opportunities

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierPaddingAllEqual$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `padding(start = x, end = x, top = x, bottom = x)` shorthand opportunities

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindModifierWeightOutsideRowColumn$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Modifier.weight(weight)` is an extension on `RowScope`/`ColumnScope` — calling it elsewhere is a compile error in well-typed code, but stub builds and intrinsic-measurement hacks let mis-scoped calls slip through. Flag any `weight(...)` on a `Modifier` chain whose nearest enclosing scoped builder isn't a `Row` or `Column`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindMutableCollectionAsComposableParam$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Compose's stability inferrer treats `MutableList`/`MutableMap`/`MutableSet` parameters as unstable — every recomposition compares by identity and re-invokes the composable even if no element changed. Use `kotlinx.collections.immutable.ImmutableList` (or wrap in a `@Stable` class) so equality checks short-circuit and recomposition is skipped.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindMutableStateInClassField$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `mutableStateOf(...)` stored in a class field
recipes.description: `private val x = mutableStateOf(...)` at class scope ties the state to the lifetime of the enclosing class — ViewModel scope is fine, but UI-layer classes shouldn't be holding state for the composable. Hoist into a ViewModel or accept the state from the caller via parameters so recomposition and lifecycle agree on ownership.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindMutableStateInComposableWithoutRemember$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A bare `mutableStateOf(...)` call inside a `@Composable` allocates a fresh `MutableState` on every recomposition, throwing away the previous value. Wrap in `remember { mutableStateOf(...) }` so the snapshot survives recomposition (or hoist into a ViewModel if it needs to survive process death).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindNavigateInComposableBody$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `navController.navigate(...)` called directly in the body fires on every recomposition, leading to navigation loops or back-stack corruption. Wrap in a `LaunchedEffect(key) { … }` keyed by the condition that should trigger the navigation, or move the call into an event handler (`onClick = { … }`).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindNonComposableUsingComposableApis$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A function that calls `LaunchedEffect`/`remember`/`rememberCoroutineScope` but isn't annotated `@Composable` itself is a compile error in well-typed code, but suppressors and hand-rolled annotations let it slip through. Add `@Composable` to the function declaration so the contract is explicit.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindObserveAsState$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `observeAsState()` ties subscription to the composition, not to the lifecycle owner — collection keeps running while the host activity is `STOPPED`. Migrate to `StateFlow` and `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` (or stay on LiveData and use `androidx.lifecycle.compose.observeAsState`, which is lifecycle-aware in newer versions).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindPublicMutableStateFlowProperty$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Convention pattern: `private val _state = MutableStateFlow(...); val state: StateFlow<T> = _state.asStateFlow()`. A non-`private` `MutableStateFlow` property exposes the writable handle to consumers — anyone who can read it can also call `.value = …` or `tryEmit(...)`, breaking the unidirectional-data-flow contract the ViewModel is supposed to enforce. Make the field `private` and expose a read-only `StateFlow` view.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindRecompositionSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Recomposition-related patterns whose default behavior surprises authors: `LazyColumn`/`LazyRow`/`LazyVerticalGrid` whose inner `items(...)` calls have no `key` (composition state churns on reorder), and lazy-list content lambdas that read snapshot state from the enclosing scope (every state change invalidates the entire list).

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLazyColumnDirectCall$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `LazyColumn { … }` calls — verify items use stable keys

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.compose.FindLazyRowDirectCall$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `LazyRow { … }` calls — verify items use stable keys
