recipes.description: With kotlin-logging's lambda form (`log.trace { "..." }`) the level-check is built into the call — wrapping it in `if (log.isTraceEnabled)` repeats the check. With SLF4J's parameterized form, the placeholder substitution is also deferred, so the explicit guard is only worthwhile if the argument construction itself is expensive.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindIsWarnEnabledGuard$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Warning logs are nearly always enabled. The guard is almost certainly dead code — drop it and use the parameterized form.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindJulLoggerGetLogger$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.logging` ships with the JDK but lacks the structured-logging, MDC, and parameterized-message ergonomics of SLF4J or kotlin-logging. Migrate `j.u.l.Logger.getLogger(...)` to `LoggerFactory.getLogger(...)` (SLF4J) or `KotlinLogging.logger { }` (kotlin-logging).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindJulLoggerLog$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `j.u.l.Logger.log(Level, ...)` call (and the level-specific shortcuts `fine`/`info`/`warning`/`severe`/`config`) needs to be re-expressed against SLF4J/kotlin-logging when migrating. Flag for review.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLegacyLoggerLibraries$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Bundles `java.util.logging` and log4j 1.x finders. Both predate structured logging and should migrate to SLF4J or kotlin-logging.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLog4j1Logger$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Log4j 1.x reached end-of-life in 2015 and has known unfixed vulnerabilities. Migrate to log4j 2.x (`org.apache.logging.log4j.Logger`) or SLF4J. The migration is mechanical for the basic getLogger / log methods, but custom appenders and layouts need a manual rewrite.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLoggerDeclarationSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Bundles `log` vs `logger` naming, missing `private` on companion-object loggers, and instance-field loggers (one per allocation). The shape consensus is `private val log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(...)` in a companion object.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLoggerNotInCompanion$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find loggers declared as instance fields (one per object)

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLoggerFactoryGetLogger$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `LoggerFactory.getLogger(Foo::class.java)` is the Java idiom Kotlin code inherited. kotlin-logging's `KotlinLogging.logger { }` infers the enclosing class automatically (via the stack frame at site of declaration) and avoids the `::class.java` reflection round-trip.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLoggerFactoryGetLoggerWithStringName$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A string logger name is fine for named/structured loggers but is a smell when the string happens to spell out a class FQN — that should be `getLogger(Foo::class.java)` (or `KotlinLogging.logger { }`) so renames track. Flag for human review.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLoggerFactoryGetLoggerWithThisClass$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `this::class.java` resolves the runtime class — fine for non-final classes, but kotlin-logging's `KotlinLogging.logger { }` already infers the declaring class lexically and avoids the runtime reflection. Either form binds the same logger name for a final class.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLoggerFactoryMigrationCandidates$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Bundles the SLF4J `LoggerFactory.getLogger` shapes — class-literal, `this::class.java`, and string-name. Each is a candidate for kotlin-logging's `KotlinLogging.logger { }`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLoggerFieldNamedLog$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Both `log` and `logger` are common — pick one and stick with it across the codebase. The naming convention is the only thing that lets a reader skim a file and spot the logger declaration in two seconds. Flag `log`-named declarations so the team can confirm the project convention.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLoggerGuards$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Bundles `if (log.isXxxEnabled) ...` finders. With kotlin-logging's lambda form or SLF4J's `{}` placeholder form, the level check is built into the call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindLoggerNotInCompanion$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find loggers declared as instance fields (one per object)
recipes.description: An instance-field `val log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(...)` allocates one logger per object. Logger factories cache by name, so the runtime cost is one extra map lookup per allocation — but the conventional shape is a `private val log` in the companion object (or a top-level `private val log` for top-level functions), so a per-instance logger usually reflects accidental code placement.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindPrintAndPrintStackTrace$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Bundles the unstructured-output finders. Each call writes outside the logger pipeline, so it bypasses level filters, MDCs, and structured sinks.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindPrintErr$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `System.err.println` writes to stderr — better than stdout for errors, but still bypasses whatever structured logger the application uses. Route through `log.error("...", throwable)` so log aggregators see the context.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindPrintln$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `println` writes to stdout, which in containerized deployments lands in log files without structure, level filtering, or correlation IDs. Replace with a proper logger; if this is a CLI tool, consider the kotlin-logging level filter so tests can silence noisy output.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindPrintStackTrace$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `e.printStackTrace()` writes the throwable's stack frames straight to `System.err`, bypassing whatever logger the application configures. Use `log.error("context", e)` so the throwable flows through SLF4J's last-arg-is-Throwable convention and ends up in the same sink as the rest of your errors.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindStringConcatInLogDebug$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `log.debug("x=" + x)` performs the concatenation eagerly. Use kotlin-logging's `log.debug { "x=$x" }` lambda form or SLF4J's `log.debug("x={}", x)` placeholder form.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindStringConcatInLogError$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `log.error("failed: " + e)` mixes the throwable into the message string, losing the stack trace. Use the parameterized form with the throwable as the last argument: `log.error("failed", e)`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindStringConcatInLogInfo$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `log.info("x=" + x)` is the Java-1.4-era logging idiom — replaced in SLF4J by `log.info("x={}", x)` so the template is stable and the work is deferred.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindStringConcatInLogTrace$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `log.trace("x=" + x)` performs the concatenation (and the `toString` on `x`) before the call — wasted work if trace is disabled. Use the lambda form or SLF4J `{}` placeholders.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindStringConcatInLogWarn$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `log.warn("x=" + x)` does the concatenation up front. Use the parameterized form so log aggregators can group by message template.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.FindThrowablePrintStackTraceWithStream$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Writing the stack trace to a `PrintStream` / `PrintWriter` is the Java idiom for re-routing it manually. With a structured logger you don't need to — `log.error("context", e)` already carries the throwable to the configured sink. Review whether the explicit redirection still serves a purpose.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.logging.Logging$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Search-only recipes for SLF4J, kotlin-logging, `java.util.logging`, log4j 1.x, and `println`/`printStackTrace` usage. Covers eager-message construction (string templates and concatenation), redundant level-check guards, `LoggerFactory.getLogger` shapes that could be `KotlinLogging.logger { }`, unstructured-output calls that bypass the logger, and logger-declaration smells (naming, visibility, instance-field placement).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.Kotlin1To2$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Modernizes a Kotlin 1.x codebase for Kotlin 2.x: replaces stdlib APIs deprecated between 1.4 and 2.0 with their modern equivalents, swaps JVM-only `java.lang`/`java.util` helpers for multiplatform Kotlin extensions, migrates `inline class` to `@JvmInline value class`, and removes `@OptIn` annotations for experimental markers that have since graduated to stable.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinNumberApis$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Use Kotlin number extensions instead of `java.lang.Integer`/`Long`/`Double`/`Float`/`Boolean`

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinCollections$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Use Kotlin collection extensions instead of `java.util.Collections`

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinArray$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Use Kotlin array extensions instead of `java.util.Arrays`

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseValueClass$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Use `@JvmInline value class` instead of `inline class`

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.RemoveDeprecatedKotlinGradleProperties
recipes.description: Remove deprecated Kotlin Gradle properties from `gradle.properties`. `kotlin.experimental.coroutines` was removed in Kotlin 2.x.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.RemoveRedundantKotlinStdlib
recipes.description: Remove explicit `kotlin-stdlib`, `kotlin-stdlib-jdk7`, `kotlin-stdlib-jdk8`, and `kotlin-stdlib-common` dependencies. The Kotlin Gradle plugin has automatically included the stdlib since Kotlin 1.4, making explicit declarations redundant.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.RemoveRedundantOptIns$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Removes `@OptIn` annotations for stdlib experimental markers that have since graduated to stable (`ExperimentalStdlibApi`, `ExperimentalTime`, `ExperimentalUnsignedTypes`, `ExperimentalPathApi`). The annotations no longer suppress anything and just add noise.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.RenameKotlinOptionsToCompilerOptions
recipes.description: Rename the deprecated `kotlinOptions` DSL block to `compilerOptions` in Gradle build files (Groovy and Kotlin DSL). The `kotlinOptions` DSL was deprecated in Kotlin 2.0 and removed in Kotlin 2.2. Note: in the Kotlin DSL the assignments inside the block must also be modernized for the result to compile; see `UseJvmTargetProviderSyntax` and `UseFreeCompilerArgsAddAll`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.ReplaceDeprecatedAppendln
recipes.description: Replace `appendln()` with `appendLine()`. This was deprecated in Kotlin 1.4 and becomes an error in Kotlin 2.1.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.ReplaceDeprecatedCapitalizeAndDecapitalize
recipes.description: Replace `String.capitalize()` with `String.replaceFirstChar { if (it.isLowerCase()) it.titlecase() else it.toString() }` and `String.decapitalize()` with `String.replaceFirstChar { it.lowercase() }`. These were deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 and become errors in Kotlin 2.1.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.ReplaceDeprecatedCharCaseConversions
recipes.description: Replace `Char.toLowerCase()` with `Char.lowercaseChar()` and `Char.toUpperCase()` with `Char.uppercaseChar()`. These were deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 and become errors in Kotlin 2.1.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.ReplaceDeprecatedStringCaseConversions
recipes.description: Replace `String.toLowerCase()` with `String.lowercase()` and `String.toUpperCase()` with `String.uppercase()`. These were deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 and become errors in Kotlin 2.1.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.ReplaceEnumValuesFunctionWithEnumEntries
recipes.description: Replace calls to `enumValues<T>()` with `enumEntries<T>()`. The `enumEntries` function returns an efficient immutable list instead of creating a new array. Deprecated since Kotlin 1.9, recommended replacement for Kotlin 2.x.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.ReplaceEnumValuesWithEntries
recipes.description: Replace calls to `Enum.values()` with the `Enum.entries` property. The `entries` property returns an efficient immutable list instead of creating a new array on each call. Deprecated since Kotlin 1.9, recommended replacement for Kotlin 2.x.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.ReplaceKotlinOptionsWithCompilerOptions
recipes.displayName: Replace `kotlinOptions` with `compilerOptions` in Gradle build files
recipes.description: Migrate the deprecated `kotlinOptions` DSL block to `compilerOptions` in Gradle build files (Groovy and Kotlin DSL). Renames the block and, in the Kotlin DSL, modernizes the assignments inside it to the Provider-style setters (`jvmTarget.set(JvmTarget.JVM_X)`, `freeCompilerArgs.addAll(...)`) so the result compiles against the `compilerOptions` DSL. The `kotlinOptions` DSL was deprecated in Kotlin 2.0 and removed in Kotlin 2.2.

recipeList.displayName: Use the `jvmTarget` provider syntax in Kotlin `compilerOptions`

recipes.description: Upgrade all `org.jetbrains.kotlin.*` Gradle plugins to Kotlin 2.x. This includes the core kotlin-jvm plugin as well as all official Kotlin Gradle plugins such as serialization, Spring, allopen, noarg, JPA, and parcelize.

recipes.description: Migrate deprecated Kotlin 1.x APIs to their Kotlin 2.x replacements and update Gradle build files for Kotlin 2.x compatibility. Deprecated APIs were deprecated in Kotlin 1.4-1.5 and become errors in Kotlin 2.1.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseAppendLine$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Appendable.appendln()` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.4 in favor of `appendLine()` (consistent naming with `Reader.readLine()`).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseAppendLineAny$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `StringBuilder.appendln(value: Any?)` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.4 in favor of `appendLine(value: Any?)`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseAppendLineChar$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Appendable.appendln(value: Char)` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.4 in favor of `appendLine(value: Char)`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseAppendLineCharSequence$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Appendable.appendln(value: CharSequence?)` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.4 in favor of `appendLine(value: CharSequence?)`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseAppendLineWithValue$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Appendable.appendln(value)` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.4 in favor of `appendLine(value)`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseArrayContentDeepEquals$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.deepEquals(a, b)` recursively compares nested arrays; `a.contentDeepEquals(b)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseArrayContentDeepHashCode$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.deepHashCode(arr)` recursively hashes nested arrays; `arr.contentDeepHashCode()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseArrayContentDeepToString$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.deepToString(arr)` recursively unrolls nested arrays; `arr.contentDeepToString()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension producing the same representation.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseArrayContentEquals$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.equals(a: Object[], b: Object[])` is JVM-only; `a.contentEquals(b)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension. For nested arrays use the deep variant.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseArrayContentHashCode$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.hashCode(arr: Object[])` is JVM-only; `arr.contentHashCode()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension. For nested arrays use the deep variant.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseArrayContentToString$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.toString(arr: Object[])` is JVM-only; `arr.contentToString()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension. For nested arrays use the deep variant.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseBooleanArrayContentEquals$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.equals(a: boolean[], b: boolean[])` is JVM-only; `a.contentEquals(b)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseBooleanArrayContentHashCode$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.hashCode(arr: boolean[])` is JVM-only; `arr.contentHashCode()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseBooleanArrayContentToString$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.toString(arr: boolean[])` is JVM-only; `arr.contentToString()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseBooleanArrayCopyOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.copyOf(arr: boolean[], newLength)` is JVM-only; `arr.copyOf(newLength)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseBooleanArrayFill$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.fill(arr: boolean[], value)` is JVM-only; `arr.fill(value)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseByteArrayBinarySearch$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.binarySearch(arr: byte[], key: Byte)` is JVM-only; `arr.binarySearch(key)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseByteArrayContentEquals$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.equals(a: byte[], b: byte[])` is JVM-only; `a.contentEquals(b)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseByteArrayContentHashCode$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.hashCode(arr: byte[])` is JVM-only; `arr.contentHashCode()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseByteArrayContentToString$KtRecipe

recipes.description: Prefer the multiplatform-friendly `kotlin.math.hypot` over the JVM-only `Math.hypot`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathLn$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Math.log` is natural log; the multiplatform `kotlin.math` package spells it `ln` to disambiguate from `log(b, x)` (log base b).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathLn1p$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Math.log1p(x)` computes `ln(1 + x)`. The multiplatform `kotlin.math` package spells it `ln1p`, mirroring the `log`→`ln` rename.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathLog10$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prefer the multiplatform-friendly `kotlin.math.log10` over the JVM-only `Math.log10`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathMax$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prefer the multiplatform-friendly `kotlin.math.max` over the JVM-only `Math.max`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathMin$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prefer the multiplatform-friendly `kotlin.math.min` over the JVM-only `Math.min`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathPi$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prefer the multiplatform-friendly `kotlin.math.PI` over the JVM-only `Math.PI`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathSign$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Math.signum(x)` is renamed to `kotlin.math.sign(x)` in the multiplatform `kotlin.math` package.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathSin$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prefer the multiplatform-friendly `kotlin.math.sin` over the JVM-only `Math.sin`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathSinh$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prefer the multiplatform-friendly `kotlin.math.sinh` over the JVM-only `Math.sinh`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathSqrt$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prefer the multiplatform-friendly `kotlin.math.sqrt` over the JVM-only `Math.sqrt`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathTan$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prefer the multiplatform-friendly `kotlin.math.tan` over the JVM-only `Math.tan`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinMathTanh$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prefer the multiplatform-friendly `kotlin.math.tanh` over the JVM-only `Math.tanh`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinNumberApis$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Use Kotlin number extensions instead of `java.lang.Integer`/`Long`/`Double`/`Float`/`Boolean`
recipes.description: Replaces JVM-only static helpers on boxed primitive types with their multiplatform Kotlin counterparts: parsing (`s.toInt()`, `s.toLong(radix)`, `s.toDouble()`, `s.toBoolean()`), formatting (`i.toString(2)`, `l.toString(16)`), bit operations (`i.countOneBits()`, `l.rotateLeft(n)`), constants (`Int.MIN_VALUE`), and `compareTo`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseKotlinRegex$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Replaces JVM-only `java.util.regex.Pattern` calls with their multiplatform Kotlin equivalents: `s.toRegex()` and `Regex.escape(s)`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseListOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Collections.singletonList(x)` is JVM-only; Kotlin's multiplatform `listOf(x)` produces an immutable single-element list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseListReverse$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Collections.reverse(list)` is JVM-only; Kotlin's `MutableList.reverse()` extension is multiplatform and reads as a receiver call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseListShuffle$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Collections.shuffle(list)` is JVM-only; Kotlin's `MutableList.shuffle()` extension is multiplatform and reads as a receiver call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseListSort$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Collections.sort(list)` is JVM-only; Kotlin's `MutableList.sort()` extension is multiplatform and reads as a receiver call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLocalizedMessage$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Prefer the i18n-aware `localizedMessage` property over `message` when surfacing exception text to end users. Both are Kotlin properties on `java.lang.Throwable` — the rewrite is a pure property-access rename.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongArrayBinarySearch$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.binarySearch(arr: long[], key: Long)` is JVM-only; `arr.binarySearch(key)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongArrayContentEquals$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.equals(a: long[], b: long[])` is JVM-only; `a.contentEquals(b)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongArrayContentHashCode$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.hashCode(arr: long[])` is JVM-only; `arr.contentHashCode()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongArrayContentToString$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.toString(arr: long[])` is JVM-only; `arr.contentToString()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongArrayCopyOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.copyOf(arr: long[], newLength)` is JVM-only; `arr.copyOf(newLength)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongArrayFill$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.fill(arr: long[], value)` is JVM-only; `arr.fill(value)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongArraySort$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.sort(arr: long[])` is JVM-only; `arr.sort()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongCountOneBits$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Long.bitCount(l)` is the JVM-only popcount; the multiplatform `l.countOneBits()` extension reads as a receiver call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongFloorDiv$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Math.floorDiv(a, b)` becomes `a.floorDiv(b)` — the multiplatform Kotlin extension on `Long`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongMod$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Math.floorMod(a, b)` becomes `a.mod(b)` for the `(Long, Long)` overload. Kotlin's `Long.mod` matches `Math.floorMod` floored-division semantics.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongModInt$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Math.floorMod(a: Long, b: Int): Int` becomes `a.mod(b)`. Like the Java overload, `Long.mod(Int)` returns an `Int`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongRotateLeft$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.lang.Long.rotateLeft(l, n)` is JVM-only; the multiplatform `l.rotateLeft(n)` extension reads as a receiver call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongRotateRight$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.lang.Long.rotateRight(l, n)` is JVM-only; the multiplatform `l.rotateRight(n)` extension reads as a receiver call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongToString$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.lang.Long.toString(l)` is the JVM-only spelling; `l.toString()` reads as a receiver call and is multiplatform.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLongToStringWithRadix$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.lang.Long.toString(l, radix)` is the JVM-only spelling; `l.toString(radix)` is the multiplatform Kotlin receiver call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLowercase$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `String.toLowerCase()` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 in favor of the locale-explicit `lowercase()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLowercaseChar$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Char.toLowerCase()` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 in favor of the locale-explicit `lowercaseChar()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseLowercaseWithLocale$KtRecipe
recipes.description: The JVM `String.toLowerCase(Locale)` overload was deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 alongside the no-arg form; the replacement `lowercase(Locale)` keeps the locale parameter and uses the new spelling.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseModernKotlinStdlibApis$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Replaces Kotlin stdlib APIs deprecated between 1.4 and 2.0 with their modern equivalents, and adopts newer language features (open-ended range `..<`, `enumEntries<T>()`) where the older spelling still compiles but reads worse.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseRangeUntilOperator$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Kotlin 1.7.20 introduced the `..<` open-ended range operator. Prefer it over the older `until` infix function.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseReadln$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Kotlin 1.6 introduced `readln()` to replace the common `readLine()!!` idiom — the new spelling makes the EOF-throws contract explicit and drops the not-null assertion.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseReadlnOrNull$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `readLine()` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.6 in favor of `readlnOrNull()` (and the asserting `readln()`), which spells the EOF-handling intent explicitly.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseRegexEscape$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.regex.Pattern.quote(s)` migrates to `kotlin.text.Regex.escape(s)` — same behavior, multiplatform.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseRemoveAtLastIndexForRemoveLast$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `MutableList.removeLast()` was deprecated in Kotlin 2.0 alongside `removeFirst()` for the same SequencedCollection conflict. Prefer `removeAt(lastIndex)`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseRemoveAtZeroForRemoveFirst$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `MutableList.removeFirst()` was deprecated in Kotlin 2.0 because Java 21's `SequencedCollection.removeFirst()` introduced a conflicting signature with different return-on-empty semantics. Prefer `removeAt(0)` to keep the throwing behavior unambiguous.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseSetOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Collections.singleton(x)` is JVM-only; Kotlin's multiplatform `setOf(x)` produces an immutable single-element set.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseShortArrayBinarySearch$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.binarySearch(arr: short[], key: Short)` is JVM-only; `arr.binarySearch(key)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseShortArrayContentEquals$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.equals(a: short[], b: short[])` is JVM-only; `a.contentEquals(b)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseShortArrayContentHashCode$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.hashCode(arr: short[])` is JVM-only; `arr.contentHashCode()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseShortArrayContentToString$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.toString(arr: short[])` is JVM-only; `arr.contentToString()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseShortArrayCopyOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.copyOf(arr: short[], newLength)` is JVM-only; `arr.copyOf(newLength)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseShortArrayFill$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.fill(arr: short[], value)` is JVM-only; `arr.fill(value)` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseShortArraySort$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.Arrays.sort(arr: short[])` is JVM-only; `arr.sort()` is the multiplatform Kotlin extension.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseStringToBoolean$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Java-idiom `Boolean.parseBoolean(s)` migrates to the Kotlin extension `s.toBoolean()`; for strict parsing that throws on non-`true`/`false`, use `s.toBooleanStrict()` instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseStringToDouble$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Java-idiom `Double.parseDouble(s)` migrates to the Kotlin extension `s.toDouble()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseStringToFloat$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Java-idiom `Float.parseFloat(s)` migrates to the Kotlin extension `s.toFloat()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseStringToInt$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Java-idiom `Integer.parseInt(s)` migrates to the Kotlin extension `s.toInt()`. The behavior is identical — both throw `NumberFormatException` on invalid input.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseStringToIntWithRadix$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Integer.parseInt(s, radix)` is JVM-only; the Kotlin extension `s.toInt(radix)` is multiplatform and reads as a receiver call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseStringToLong$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Java-idiom `Long.parseLong(s)` migrates to the Kotlin extension `s.toLong()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseStringToLongWithRadix$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.lang.Long.parseLong(s, radix)` is JVM-only; the Kotlin extension `s.toLong(radix)` is multiplatform and reads as a receiver call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseStringToRegex$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.util.regex.Pattern.compile(s)` migrates to the Kotlin extension `s.toRegex()`, which returns a `kotlin.text.Regex` and reads more naturally.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseSumOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Iterable.sumBy { … }` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 in favor of the type-inferred `sumOf { … }` (which avoids the unchecked Int return).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseSumOfDouble$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Iterable.sumByDouble { … }` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 in favor of the type-inferred `sumOf { … }`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseUppercase$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `String.toUpperCase()` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 in favor of the locale-explicit `uppercase()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseUppercaseChar$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Char.toUpperCase()` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 in favor of the locale-explicit `uppercaseChar()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseUppercaseWithLocale$KtRecipe
recipes.description: The JVM `String.toUpperCase(Locale)` overload was deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 alongside the no-arg form; the replacement `uppercase(Locale)` keeps the locale parameter and uses the new spelling.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.migrate.UseValueClass$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Use `@JvmInline value class` instead of `inline class`
recipes.description: `inline class` was deprecated in Kotlin 1.5 in favor of the explicit `@JvmInline value class` pair; the new spelling separates the JVM mapping (`@JvmInline`) from the language-level semantics (`value`).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.OrderImports
recipes.description: Groups and orders import statements. If a [style has been defined](https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/styles), this recipe will order the imports according to that style. If no style is detected, this recipe will default to ordering imports in the same way that IntelliJ IDEA does.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.CollapseFilterTerminals$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Folds predicate-taking terminals (`first`, `last`, `count`, `any`, `none`, `single`, `firstOrNull`, `lastOrNull`, `singleOrNull`) and `sumOf`/`maxOf`/`minOf` selectors into the upstream `filter` or `map`, avoiding the intermediate list materialization.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.CollapseSortAndReverse$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Replaces O(n log n) sorts whose only purpose is to read one element with the equivalent O(n) `min`/`max`/`minBy`/`maxBy`, and elides unnecessary `reversed()` copies before `first`/`last`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindAllocationsInCollectionLambdas$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find expensive allocations inside collection lambdas
recipes.description: Search-only recipes that flag heavyweight allocations sitting inside the trailing lambda of a `map` / `filter` / `forEach` / `flatMap` call. Each such lambda runs once per element — the same allocation-cost profile as a loop body.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindObjectMapperInCollectionLambdas$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find Jackson `ObjectMapper()` allocations inside collection lambdas

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindAllocationsInHotPaths$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find expensive allocations on hot paths
recipes.description: Search-only recipes that flag heavyweight allocations sitting on a path the runtime exercises repeatedly — inside a loop, inside `View.onDraw`/`onMeasure`/`onLayout`. Each match shows up as a `SearchResult` for review; nothing is rewritten automatically.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindAllocationsInOnDraw$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Android views call `onDraw` on every frame. Allocating `Paint`, `Path`, `Rect`, `RectF`, `Region`, `Matrix`, or `Bitmap` instances per draw causes GC pressure and dropped frames — hoist them into field initializers or `lazy { }` properties.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindAllocationsInOnLayout$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `onLayout` runs whenever a view's children are repositioned. Allocating `Paint`, `Path`, `Rect`, `RectF`, `Region`, `Matrix`, or `Bitmap` instances per layout causes per-frame GC pressure — hoist them to fields.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindAllocationsInOnMeasure$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `onMeasure` runs whenever the measurement pass walks a view. Allocating `Paint`, `Path`, `Rect`, `RectF`, `Region`, `Matrix`, or `Bitmap` instances per measure makes layout reflows hit the GC — hoist them to fields.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindBase64GetDecoderInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Base64.getDecoder()` returns a shared singleton, so the call itself is cheap — but reading the decoder from a `final` field is cheaper still. Hoist the decoder to a top-level `private val` for clarity.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindBigDecimalFromStringInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Parsing a `BigDecimal` from a `String` literal inside a loop reparses the same value every iteration. Hoist the literal `BigDecimal` out of the loop or use a cached constant.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindBigIntegerFromStringInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Parsing a `BigInteger` from a `String` literal inside a loop reparses the same value every iteration. Hoist the literal `BigInteger` to a top-level property or `BigInteger.valueOf` constant.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindBigIntegerValueOfInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `BigInteger.valueOf` caches small values (-16..16) but allocates fresh `BigInteger` instances outside that range. Loop bodies frequently feed it dynamic values — hoist a constant where possible or accept the allocation cost.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindCalendarGetInstanceInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Calendar.getInstance()` resolves the default `TimeZone` and `Locale` and allocates a fresh `GregorianCalendar` on every call. Inside a loop the timezone lookup dominates — hoist the calendar or migrate to `java.time` types.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindCharsetForNameInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Charset.forName("UTF-8")` walks the charset alias map on every call. Prefer the cached constants on `kotlin.text.Charsets` (`Charsets.UTF_8`, `Charsets.ISO_8859_1`, etc.) — or hoist a single `Charset` out of the loop.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindClassForNameInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Class.forName(...)` walks the classloader hierarchy on every call. Resolving the same class on every loop iteration burns CPU — cache the resolved `Class<*>` in a top-level property.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindDateTimeFormatterInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern(...)` parses the pattern up-front. Doing that on every loop iteration burns CPU repeatedly — hoist the formatter into a top-level property. Unlike `SimpleDateFormat`, `DateTimeFormatter` is thread-safe, so the hoisted instance can be shared.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindEagerMapOnSequence$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Calling `.toList()` on a `Sequence` and then `.map { … }` materializes the full sequence into a `List` and then walks it again — defeating the lazy-pipeline purpose of `Sequence`. Drop the `toList()` so the `map` stays in the sequence.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindFileNewBufferedReaderInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Constructing a `File` and opening a `BufferedReader` per loop iteration multiplies the OS-level open/read/close cost. If the same path is read each pass, read it once before the loop; if every iteration reads a different path, batch the work or reuse a `Reader`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindForEachWithIndexedAccess$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `for (i in xs.indices) { val x = xs[i] }` patterns
recipes.description: Iterating over `xs.indices` and indexing back into `xs[i]` is the explicit-index form of `xs.forEachIndexed { i, x -> }`. The indexed form is clearer and avoids re-resolving `xs[i]` on every access.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindGsonInCollectionLambdas$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Gson's default constructor builds the type-adapter registry up front. Allocating a fresh `Gson` per element repeats that work — hoist one `Gson` instance to a top-level property.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindGsonInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Gson's default constructor builds the type-adapter registry up front. Allocating one per loop iteration repeats that work — hoist a single `Gson` instance to a top-level property.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindIterationSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Flags iteration idioms that have a clearer, allocation-equivalent Kotlin form — currently the `for (i in xs.indices) { val x = xs[i] }` shape that `forEachIndexed { i, x -> }` replaces.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindForEachWithIndexedAccess$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `for (i in xs.indices) { val x = xs[i] }` patterns

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindLargeListPipeline$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find long `List` pipelines that should use `Sequence`
recipes.description: A pipeline with three or more chained collection operations (`map`/`filter`/`flatMap`/etc.) on a `List` materializes an intermediate collection per stage. Long pipelines on large inputs typically run faster (and allocate less) as `xs.asSequence().…toList()`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindListOfInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: An immutable `listOf(...)` built inside a loop allocates a fresh list every iteration. If the contents are constant, hoist the list to a `val` outside the loop. If the contents change per iteration, the allocation is necessary — review and accept.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindLocaleConstructionInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Locale("en", "US")` walks the locale provider list on every construction. For common locales prefer the cached constants on `Locale` (e.g. `Locale.US`, `Locale.ENGLISH`). Otherwise hoist a single `Locale` out of the loop.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindLoggerFactoryGetLoggerInCollectionLambdas$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `LoggerFactory.getLogger(...)` resolves the logger through SLF4J on every call. Inside a collection lambda that resolves the same logger per element — hoist it to a `private val` companion property.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindLoggerFactoryGetLoggerInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `LoggerFactory.getLogger(...)` resolves the logger through the SLF4J binding on every call. Hoist the logger to a `private val` companion property — there's exactly one logger per class.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindLoopAllocations$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Flags `listOf` / `mutableListOf` / `mutableMapOf` calls that allocate a fresh collection on every loop iteration. Hoist constants or `clear()`-and-reuse a single instance.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindMessageDigestGetInstanceInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5")` walks the security-provider list on every call. Hoist the digest to a per-thread cache or reset it per use.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindMutableListOfInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `mutableListOf<T>()` allocated per iteration produces garbage proportional to the loop count. If the list is filled and consumed each pass, consider `clear()`-and-reuse on a single hoisted list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindMutableMapOfInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `mutableMapOf<K, V>()` allocated per iteration produces garbage proportional to the loop count. If the map is filled and consumed each pass, consider `clear()`-and-reuse on a single hoisted map.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindObjectMapperInCollectionLambdas$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find Jackson `ObjectMapper()` allocations inside collection lambdas
recipes.description: Allocating a fresh `ObjectMapper` per element rebuilds Jackson's module/serializer registry on every call. Hoist one mapper to a top-level property — it is thread-safe once configured.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindObjectMapperInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Jackson's `ObjectMapper` is expensive to construct — it builds the default module and serializer registries on every allocation. Hoist a single `ObjectMapper` instance to a top-level property; it is thread-safe once configured.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindOptionalGetInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Optional.get()` throws `NoSuchElementException` when the optional is empty — the loop body usually relies on a preceding `isPresent` check. Prefer `orElse`, `orElseThrow`, or `ifPresent { }` to make the empty branch explicit and avoid the double-check.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindPatternCompileInCollectionLambdas$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Pattern.compile(...)` parses the pattern up front; running it inside a `map`/`filter`/`forEach` lambda recompiles the pattern for every element. Hoist the `Pattern` to a top-level property.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindPatternCompileInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Compiling a `java.util.regex.Pattern` is expensive — allocating one inside a loop recompiles it on every iteration. Hoist the `Pattern` out of the loop or cache it in a top-level property.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindRegexAllocationsInCollectionLambdas$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `Regex` allocated inside the lambda passed to `map`, `filter`, `forEach`, `flatMap`, etc. is compiled once per element. Hoist the regex to a top-level property — collection-pipeline lambdas run on every element, just like a loop body.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindRegexAllocationsInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Compiling a `Regex` is expensive — allocating one inside a loop pays the cost on every iteration. Hoist the regex out of the loop or cache it in a top-level property.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindSequencePipelineSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Flags pipelines where the `List`/`Sequence` choice fights the data flow — long `List` pipelines that materialize between every stage, and `Sequence` pipelines that eagerly fall back to `List` mid-pipeline.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindLargeListPipeline$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find long `List` pipelines that should use `Sequence`

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindSimpleDateFormatInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `SimpleDateFormat` parses its pattern string in the constructor and is not thread-safe — allocating one per iteration is a common per-row hot spot. Hoist it out of the loop or use a thread-local cache (or migrate to `DateTimeFormatter`).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindStringConcatSmells$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Flags `s = s + "…"`-inside-loop patterns that allocate a fresh `String` on every iteration. The `StringBuilder.length`-vs-`size` rewrite lives in the autofix bundle.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindStringPlusInLoop$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find `s = s + "..."` string concatenation inside loops

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindStringFormatInCollectionLambdas$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `String.format(...)` reparses the format string on every call. Inside a collection lambda that runs per element — prefer Kotlin string templates (`"${x}"`) or hoist a `Formatter`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindStringFormatInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `String.format(...)` parses the format string on every call. Inside a loop this re-parses the same template every iteration — prefer string templates (`"${x}"`) or extract the `Formatter` if you must use `%`-style specifiers.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindStringPlusInLoop$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `s = s + "..."` string concatenation inside loops
recipes.description: Repeated `String` concatenation inside a loop allocates a new `String` on every iteration — each `+` produces a fresh `StringBuilder`. Prefer building once with `StringBuilder` (or `buildString { … }`).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindURIConstructorInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.net.URI`'s constructor parses and validates the URI string. Doing that per loop iteration burns CPU on the same string — hoist constants out of the loop.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindURLConstructorInLoops$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `java.net.URL`'s constructor parses the URL string and dispatches through `URLStreamHandlerFactory`. Inside a loop that adds up — hoist URLs that don't change per iteration, or migrate to `URI`/`HttpRequest` builders.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.ImproveKotlinPerformance$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Autofix-only performance bundle: collapses allocating call chains (filter/map/sort/reverse), promotes Compose primitive state holders, and rewrites `StringBuilder.length` to `size`. Excludes the search-only `Find*` recipes so the run output is just diffs, not a flood of search results.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.Performance$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Opinionated bundle of every performance recipe in this module: chain collapses (filter/map/sort/reverse), Compose primitive-state holders, and hot-path allocation finders. Search-result recipes coexist with rewriting recipes — for diff-only output, use `ImproveKotlinPerformance` instead.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindAllocationsInHotPaths$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find expensive allocations on hot paths

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.FindAllocationsInCollectionLambdas$KtRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Find expensive allocations inside collection lambdas

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseAnyWithPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `any { predicate }` short-circuits on the first match and avoids materializing the intermediate filtered list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseAnyWithPredicateInsteadOfFilterAny$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `any { predicate }` short-circuits on the first match. Calling `any()` after `filter` first materializes the entire filtered list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseComposePrimitiveStateOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Inside `@Composable` functions, replaces `mutableStateOf(<primitive>)` with the matching primitive-specialized `mutableIntStateOf`/`mutableLongStateOf`/`mutableFloatStateOf`/`mutableDoubleStateOf`. The specialized state holders keep the wrapped value unboxed across reads and writes during recomposition.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseCountWithPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Folding the predicate into `count` avoids materializing the intermediate filtered list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseFilterNotToForFilterNotToMutableList$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `filterNot { p }` allocates a `List<T>` and `toMutableList` copies it. `filterNotTo(mutableListOf(), p)` writes directly into the target without the intermediate.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseFilterToForFilterToMutableList$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `filter { p }` allocates a `List<T>` and `toMutableList` copies it. `filterTo(mutableListOf(), p)` writes directly into the target without the intermediate.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseFirstForReversedLast$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `reversed()` allocates an intermediate reversed copy. `first()` returns the same element directly.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseFirstNotNullOfForMapFirst$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `firstNotNullOf` short-circuits on the first non-null result. `mapNotNull { f }.first()` walks the whole input.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseFirstNotNullOfOrNullForMapFirstOrNull$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `firstNotNullOfOrNull` short-circuits on the first non-null result. `mapNotNull { f }.firstOrNull()` walks the whole input.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseFirstOrNullWithPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Folding the predicate into `firstOrNull` short-circuits on the first match and avoids materializing the intermediate filtered list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseFirstWithPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Folding the predicate into `first` avoids materializing the intermediate filtered list and short-circuits on the first match.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseFlatMapToForFlatMapToMutableList$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `flatMap { f }` allocates a `List<R>` and `toMutableList` copies it. `flatMapTo(mutableListOf(), f)` writes directly into the target without the intermediate.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseLastForReversedFirst$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `reversed()` allocates an intermediate reversed copy. `last()` walks to the same element directly.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseLastOrNullWithPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Folding the predicate into `lastOrNull` avoids materializing the intermediate filtered list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseLastWithPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Folding the predicate into `last` avoids materializing the intermediate filtered list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseLengthForStringBuilderSize$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Calling `toString()` on a `StringBuilder` allocates a snapshot `String` just to read its length. `StringBuilder` exposes `length` directly without the copy.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMapNotNullForMapFilterNotNull$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `mapNotNull` drops nulls in the same pass that produces them. `map { f }.filterNotNull()` materializes the full `List<R?>` first.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMapToForMapToMutableList$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `map { f }` allocates a `List<R>` and `toMutableList` copies it. `mapTo(mutableListOf(), f)` writes directly into the target without the intermediate.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMaxByForSortedByLast$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `sortedBy(f).last()` does an O(n log n) sort just to read the maximum-by-`f`. `maxBy(f)` finds it in a single linear pass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMaxForSortedDescendingFirst$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `sortedDescending().first()` does an O(n log n) sort just to read the maximum. `max()` finds it in a single linear pass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMaxForSortedLast$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `sorted().last()` does an O(n log n) sort just to read the maximum. `max()` finds it in a single linear pass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMaxOfWithSelector$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `maxOf` walks the input once and tracks the running maximum without materializing the intermediate `List<Int>`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMinByForSortedByFirst$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `sortedBy(f).first()` does an O(n log n) sort just to read the minimum-by-`f`. `minBy(f)` finds it in a single linear pass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMinForSortedDescendingLast$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `sortedDescending().last()` does an O(n log n) sort just to read the minimum. `min()` finds it in a single linear pass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMinForSortedFirst$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `sorted().first()` does an O(n log n) sort just to read the minimum. `min()` finds it in a single linear pass.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMinOfWithSelector$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `minOf` walks the input once and tracks the running minimum without materializing the intermediate `List<Int>`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMutableDoubleStateOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Compose's `mutableDoubleStateOf` keeps the wrapped value as a primitive `Double`, avoiding the autobox-and-unbox cost that `mutableStateOf<Double>` pays on every read and write inside a recomposition.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMutableFloatStateOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Compose's `mutableFloatStateOf` keeps the wrapped value as a primitive `Float`, avoiding the autobox-and-unbox cost that `mutableStateOf<Float>` pays on every read and write inside a recomposition.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMutableIntStateOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Compose's `mutableIntStateOf` keeps the wrapped value as a primitive `Int`, avoiding the autobox-and-unbox cost that `mutableStateOf<Int>` pays on every read and write inside a recomposition.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseMutableLongStateOf$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Compose's `mutableLongStateOf` keeps the wrapped value as a primitive `Long`, avoiding the autobox-and-unbox cost that `mutableStateOf<Long>` pays on every read and write inside a recomposition.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseNoneWithPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `none { predicate }` short-circuits on the first match and avoids materializing the intermediate filtered list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseNoneWithPredicateInsteadOfFilterNone$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `none { predicate }` short-circuits on the first match. Calling `none()` after `filter` first materializes the entire filtered list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseSingleOrNullWithPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Folding the predicate into `singleOrNull` avoids materializing the intermediate filtered list.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseSingleWithPredicate$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Folding the predicate into `single` avoids materializing the intermediate filtered list and preserves the same throwing semantics on the no-match and multi-match cases.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseSortedByDescendingForSortedByReversed$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `sortedByDescending` sorts directly into the target order. `sortedBy(f).reversed()` allocates an intermediate ascending-sorted list and then a reversed copy.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseSortedDescendingForSortedReversed$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `sortedDescending` sorts directly into descending order. `sorted().reversed()` allocates an intermediate ascending-sorted list and then a reversed copy.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.performance.UseSumOfWithSelector$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `sumOf` accumulates the result directly without materializing the intermediate `List<Int>`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindApiSurface$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Public `const val` / `lateinit var` declarations, `@OptIn` / `@RequiresOptIn` annotations, `@Deprecated` declarations, and JVM-interop annotations (`@JvmStatic`, `@JvmField`, `@JvmOverloads`). Each match is a position where API stability or external-consumer constraints are encoded in the source.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindAssertJChains$KtRecipe
recipes.description: AssertJ chains are the heart of the test suite's verification logic. Surfacing them helps a reviewer or LLM agent locate the assertions in a long test method and reason about coverage.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindAtomicAllocations$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Atomic primitives indicate concurrent state — each one is a place where a reviewer or LLM agent should look for happens-before reasoning. In coroutine-only code, `MutableStateFlow` or `Mutex`-guarded state is usually a clearer alternative.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindBuildHygiene$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Wildcard imports and similar source-organization smells that obscure where names come from.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindClassForName$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `Class.forName` is the entrypoint to runtime reflection — the receiver type isn't known at compile time, so type-safety analyses can't follow what happens next. Each match is a position an LLM agent should single out when reasoning about what a function can touch.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindClipboardAccess$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Clipboard reads and writes carry user data into and out of a process boundary the user typically does not associate with the app. Each call is a candidate for review of secret-leak and accidental-paste scenarios.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindCommandExecutionSinks$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Spawning a process with attacker-controlled arguments is the canonical command-injection sink. Each call here is a position where a reviewer or LLM agent should verify that the argument list is statically built or properly quoted.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindConcurrencySurface$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Raw threads, executor-service factories, JUC locks, atomic primitives, futures, synchronized blocks, `@Volatile` fields, `ThreadLocal` allocations, and JUC coordination primitives (`Semaphore`, `CountDownLatch`, `CyclicBarrier`). Each match is a position to inspect for cancellation semantics, happens-before edges, and pool lifecycle.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindCryptoSeeds$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Every cryptographic operation is a place where algorithm choice and key handling matter — `Cipher.getInstance("AES")` is not the same as `Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")`. Each match is a position for security review.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindDatabaseSeeds$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Individual SQL execution and JPA query construction calls (`Statement.executeQuery`, `Statement.executeUpdate`, `EntityManager.createQuery`). Each match is a position where a SQL/JPQL string crosses into the database layer.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindDataFlowSinks$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Locations where data crosses a trust or persistence boundary: SQL execution, filesystem writes, process execution, logger writes, outbound network, cryptographic operations, and Android clipboard access. Each match is a seed an LLM agent can connect back to upstream sources.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindDataFlowSources$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Locations where untrusted or configuration-controlled data enters the program: `readLine`/`Scanner` reads, environment/system-property reads, HTTP request reads, and filesystem reads. Each match is a seed an LLM agent (or human reviewer) can connect to downstream sinks.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindDeepNesting$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find functions with nesting depth greater than 4
recipes.description: Deeply nested control flow is the canonical hard-to-read code smell. For human reviewers and LLM agents alike, nesting beyond 4 levels signals the body should be split or flattened with early returns.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindDeprecatedDeclarations$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A `@Deprecated` declaration is API the maintainers want callers to migrate away from. Each match is a candidate to revisit either the deprecation timeline or the replacement strategy.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindEmptyCatchBlocks$KtRecipe
recipes.description: An empty `catch` block silently swallows failures — usually a bug or, at minimum, a missing comment explaining the intent. Flag for review so a reviewer or LLM agent can either log, rethrow, or document the swallow.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindEmptyFunctions$KtRecipe
recipes.description: An empty function body either belongs to a stub, an abstract-method override that intentionally does nothing, or forgotten work. For a reviewer or LLM agent reading the file, each match is a position where the contract claims something happens but nothing does.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindEntityManagerCreateQuery$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each JPA `createQuery` is a JPQL/HQL execution seed — when the query string is built from user input, the same injection class applies as for raw SQL. Flag for parameter-binding review.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindEnvironmentSources$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Environment variables and system properties are operator-controlled configuration values. Each read is a configuration seam — a reviewer or LLM agent reading the code should know which knobs the program exposes.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindExecutorServiceFactories$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `Executors.newXxx` call allocates a thread pool that needs explicit lifecycle (`shutdown` on teardown). For services that need bounded resources, each allocation is a candidate for review — and for an LLM agent, the call site reveals where the application's parallelism budget lives.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFieldReflection$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Direct field reads/writes via reflection bypass property accessors and `private` visibility. Each call is a position where invariants the surrounding code relies on can be silently violated.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFileReadBytes$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `File.readBytes` call reads a file's raw bytes into memory — useful as a filesystem-read seed and as a hint that the program holds the whole file in memory (vs. streaming).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFileReadSources$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Filesystem reads are the application's IO surface — each call is data crossing a trust boundary set by the deployment's filesystem permissions. Useful as a seed for reasoning about cold-path latency, security boundaries, and what the program depends on at runtime.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFileReadText$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `File.readText` call reads bytes off the filesystem — a trust-boundary position where the file's content becomes program data. Useful as an individual read seed for path-traversal or cold-path latency analysis.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFilesCopy$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `Files.copy` call duplicates filesystem content — flag as a write seed where source/destination path provenance and `CopyOption`s (REPLACE_EXISTING, etc.) should be reviewed.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFilesDelete$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each call deletes a file from disk — a destructive filesystem operation. Flag as a seed for review of path provenance, e.g. whether the path is attacker-controlled and whether the deletion is intentional.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFilesNewBufferedWriter$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `Files.newBufferedWriter` call opens a streaming writer to a file — a long-lived write seed where charset, `OpenOption`s, and close handling all matter.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFilesWriteString$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `java.nio.file.Files.writeString` call commits text to disk via the NIO API. Useful as an individual write seed and a position where charset and `OpenOption`s should be reviewed.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFileSystemSeeds$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Individual filesystem reads, writes, deletes, and copies via `java.io.File` and `java.nio.file.Files`. Each match is a position where the program crosses the filesystem trust boundary.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFileWriteSinks$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Filesystem writes are persistent side effects — each call is data crossing a trust boundary in the other direction. Useful as a seed for reasoning about what the application persists and where path-traversal vulnerabilities can land.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFileWriteText$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `File.writeText` call writes data to disk — a persistent side effect at the application's IO boundary. Useful as an individual write seed for path-traversal or trust-boundary analysis.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindFutureAllocations$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `CompletableFuture` (and `FutureTask`) interleave with their own thread pool; from Kotlin, `Deferred`/`async` integrates with structured concurrency. Each allocation is a candidate to migrate or at minimum to review for cancellation handling.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindGenericExceptionCatch$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Catching `Exception` or `Throwable` is almost always too broad — it sweeps up `NullPointerException`, `IllegalStateException`, and `OutOfMemoryError` into one branch. Narrow the catch to the specific exception types the block actually handles.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindGodClasses$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find classes with more than 25 methods
recipes.description: A class with this many methods has likely accreted responsibility over time. Flag for splitting along the methods' natural seams — repository vs mapper, view-model vs presenter, etc.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindHardcodedColorLiterals$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Hardcoded ARGB literals inside `Color(0xFF...)` calls are a design-token leak — they should usually live in a theme or material color scheme. Each match is a candidate to extract to `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.X`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindHardcodedLiterals$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find hardcoded literals and error-handling smells
recipes.description: Hardcoded design tokens (`Color(0xFF...)`), empty `catch` blocks, overly-broad `catch (e: Exception)` clauses, and `throw RuntimeException(...)` calls. Each match is a position where intent is unclear or recovery is too broad.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindHotspots$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Surface large classes, long functions, wide parameter lists, sprawling `when` expressions, deep nesting, god classes, magic numbers, and unmarked self-recursion. Each match is a candidate for a reviewer (or LLM agent) to refactor or to read carefully when building a mental model of the file.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindHttpClientConstructions$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each HTTP client construction is a place where connection pooling, timeouts, retry policy, and TLS settings are committed. Flag for review so a reviewer or LLM agent can confirm the call site picks the right policy rather than the defaults.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindHttpRequestSources$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Servlet-API request reads return raw, attacker-controlled strings. Each call is a taint root — anywhere the returned value flows into an SQL query, a filesystem path, or HTML output is a candidate vulnerability the reviewer should trace.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindHttpURLConnection$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `HttpURLConnection` is the JVM's built-in HTTP client — each reference is a position where external HTTP traffic is configured (timeouts, redirects, request method). Flag as an outbound-network seed.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindIgnoredTests$KtRecipe
recipes.description: An ignored test is a regression-detection gap — at minimum it represents technical debt; at worst it's a silenced failure that turned chronic. Each match is a candidate to triage.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindInsecureRandomSources$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Non-cryptographic randomness is fine for jitter, simulation, sampling — but each call is a position to verify that no security-relevant value (session token, password reset link, nonce) flows from it. Use `SecureRandom` instead in those positions.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindJacksonObjectMapperReadValue$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `readValue` is a JSON-deserialization sink — when the input bytes are attacker-controlled, the configured polymorphic-typing and visibility settings of the `ObjectMapper` become security-relevant. Flag as a deserialization seed.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindJacksonObjectMapperWriteValue$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `writeValue` / `writeValueAsString` / `writeValueAsBytes` call serializes a Kotlin object to JSON — useful as a seed for tracking which types cross the JSON boundary (DTO surface) and where sensitive fields might leak.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindJvmFieldAnnotations$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `@JvmField` exposes a Kotlin property as a public Java field — bypassing the generated getter/setter and freezing the storage layout in the binary API. Each match is a constraint on future refactors.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindJvmOverloadsAnnotations$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `@JvmOverloads` emits N synthetic Java overloads for a Kotlin function with default parameters. Each annotation is a hint the function is part of the Java-facing surface; reordering parameters or changing defaults breaks the synthetic overloads.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindJvmStaticAnnotations$KtRecipe
recipes.description: `@JvmStatic` declares a member function that should appear as a JVM static — a Java-interop affordance. Each annotation is a hint that the API is consumed from Java code, which constrains how it can evolve.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindKClassConstructors$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Reflective access to `KClass.constructors` reveals every constructor of a Kotlin class at runtime. Each match is a seed where reflective allocation is plausible — opaque to static analysis.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindKClassDeclaredFunctions$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Access to `KClass.declaredFunctions` (and its variants) walks every declared function of a Kotlin class via reflection. Each call is a reflection seed — opaque to static analysis and requires `kotlin-reflect.jar` at runtime.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindKClassMembers$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Access to `KClass.members` (and its sibling reflective collections) requires `kotlin-reflect.jar` at runtime and walks every declared member of the class. Each call is a position where reflection over a Kotlin type is happening — opaque to static analysis.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindKClassMembersAccess$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Kotlin reflection (`kotlin.reflect.*`) needs `kotlin-reflect.jar` on the classpath and adds significant cold-start cost. Each call is also a reflective dispatch — invisible to static analysis — so a reviewer/agent should know it's there.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindKotestSpecs$KtRecipe
recipes.description: A class extending a Kotest spec (`FunSpec`, `BehaviorSpec`, etc.) is a test entrypoint. Listing them helps a reviewer or LLM agent map a module's test surface without crawling annotations.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindLargeClasses$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find classes with more than 200 statements
recipes.description: Large classes accumulate responsibility — they bury invariants and slow every cross-cutting edit. As LLM context, an oversized class dominates the window with details that may not be relevant to the task; flagging them helps a reviewer (or an agent) decide where to split.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindLargeWhenBranches$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find `when` expressions with more than 10 branches
recipes.description: A `when` with many branches is often hiding a sealed-class or strategy-table refactor — and even when it isn't, it's a hotspot a reviewer or LLM agent should see when scanning a file. Each match is a candidate for restructuring.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindLogWriteSinks$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Logger calls can persistently capture user-controlled data into log aggregators — a PII-leak seed. Each match is a candidate to verify that the format arguments don't include sensitive fields or that a redaction layer wraps the call.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindLongFunctions$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find functions with more than 30 statements
recipes.description: Long functions hide branching and are harder to test, refactor, and reason about. For an LLM agent reading the file, an oversized body eats tokens disproportionately and obscures the contract — flag for review or extraction.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindMagicNumbers$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Magic numbers in code hide units, bounds, and protocol constants from a reader. Each match is a candidate to extract to a named `const val` so a reviewer or LLM agent can see the intent (`MAX_RETRIES`, `BUFFER_BYTES`, etc.) rather than the bare literal.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindManyParameters$KtRecipe
recipes.displayName: Find functions with more than 5 parameters
recipes.description: A long parameter list usually signals a missing aggregate (data class, builder, parameter object). For a reviewer or LLM agent, the parameter signature is the contract — when it's too wide, the call sites become hard to read and refactor in lockstep.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindMethodInvoke$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Calls through `Method.invoke` are reflective dispatch — the target body is opaque to static analysis. Flag for review whenever a reader needs to know which functions are actually reachable.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindMockkAllocations$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `mockk` allocation is a test-time fake — the production type it stands in for is the seam under test. Flagging them helps a reviewer or LLM agent see what is real and what is faked inside a test.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindNetworkingSeeds$KtRecipe
recipes.description: HTTP client and connection construction sites: `HttpURLConnection`, `okhttp3.OkHttpClient`, `okhttp3.Request.Builder`. Each match is a position where the program reaches out to the network.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindNetworkSinks$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Outbound network calls are SSRF candidates whenever the URL or request body flows from a request parameter. Each match is a seed for tracing where the program reaches into the outside world.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindNotNullAssertions$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Each `!!` is a runtime promise — when the receiver turns out to be `null`, the program crashes with a `NullPointerException`. A reviewer or LLM agent reading the code should know which positions are betting against the type system; many of them are candidates for `?.let { … }` or a `requireNotNull` with a better diagnostic.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.kotlin.search.FindObjectOutputStreamWriteObject$KtRecipe
recipes.description: Java serialization is brittle and a known security hazard on the read side; the write side is a seed where the on-wire/on-disk format gets fixed. Flag for review when migrating away from Java serialization.
