recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.AvoidEmptyCatchBlock
recipes.description: Finds catch blocks that contain no statements, which silently swallow exceptions.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.AvoidSystemExit
recipes.description: Finds `System.exit` and `sys.exit` calls which terminate the JVM. Avoid using these in library code; prefer exceptions or controlled shutdown.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.EncapsulateField
recipes.description: Finds public `var` fields in classes. Public mutable fields break encapsulation; consider using a private var with accessor methods.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.ExternalizeCredentials
recipes.description: Finds variable declarations whose name contains credential-related keywords (password, secret, token, apikey, api_key) with a non-empty string literal initializer. Hardcoded credentials are a security risk.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.ExternalizeTimeout
recipes.description: Finds hardcoded timeout values such as `Duration(5, ...)`, `5.seconds`, or `Timeout(...)` with numeric literals. Consider making timeouts configurable.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.ExtractMagicNumber
recipes.displayName: Extract magic numbers to named constants
recipes.description: Finds magic numbers (literal integers other than -1, 0, 1, 2) used in expressions or method arguments. Consider extracting them to named constants.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.InventoryScalaLogging
recipes.description: Finds imports of the Typesafe scala-logging library (`com.typesafe.scalalogging`). Use this recipe to inventory logging framework usage across a codebase.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.InventoryTypesafeConfig
recipes.description: Finds imports of the Typesafe Config library (`com.typesafe.config`). Use this recipe to inventory configuration library usage across a codebase.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.KeepClassesSmall
recipes.description: Finds classes with more than 30 members. Large classes are harder to maintain; consider splitting into smaller classes.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.KeepMethodsShort
recipes.description: Finds methods with more than 20 statements. Long methods are harder to understand and maintain; consider refactoring.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.PatchLog4j
recipes.displayName: Ensure Log4j is patched against CVE-2021-44228
recipes.description: Finds imports of Log4j 1.x (`org.apache.log4j`) or Log4j 2.x (`org.apache.logging.log4j`). Ensure your Log4j version is patched against CVE-2021-44228.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.PreferExplicitImports
recipes.description: Finds wildcard imports (`import foo._` or `import foo.*`). Explicit imports are generally preferred for clarity.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.PreferImmutableCollections
recipes.description: Replaces imports of `scala.collection.mutable.*` with `scala.collection.immutable.*`. Idiomatic Scala prefers immutable collections.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.PreferImmutableVal
recipes.description: Finds mutable `var` declarations in Scala code. Idiomatic Scala prefers immutable `val` over mutable `var`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.PreferOption
recipes.description: Replaces `null` literal with `None`. Idiomatic Scala uses `Option` instead of null.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.PreferPatternMatch
recipes.description: Finds `.asInstanceOf[T]` type casts that should be replaced with pattern matching. Idiomatic Scala prefers pattern matching over explicit casts.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.PreferPatternMatchOverInstanceOf
recipes.description: Finds `if` statements that check `isInstanceOf` in the condition and use `asInstanceOf` in the then-part. Replace with pattern matching for idiomatic Scala.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.PreferScalaPropertyAccess
recipes.displayName: Prefer Scala-style property access over Java getters
recipes.description: Finds Java-style getter methods (`getName`, `getValue`, etc.) that could be replaced with Scala-style property access.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.PreferSpecificTypes
recipes.description: Finds variable declarations whose type expression contains `Any`. Type `Any` is the Scala equivalent of `Object` and is usually too broad.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.PreferStringInterpolation
recipes.description: Finds string concatenation using the `+` operator. Idiomatic Scala prefers string interpolation (e.g., `s"hello $name"`) over concatenation with `+`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.ReduceNesting
recipes.displayName: Reduce deep nesting by extracting methods
recipes.description: Finds `def` methods with deeply nested code (5+ indentation levels). Deeply nested code is hard to follow; consider extracting methods.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.ReduceParameterCount
recipes.description: Finds `def` methods with more than 5 parameters. Long parameter lists hurt readability; consider using a case class.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.RemoveExplicitReturn
recipes.description: Removes explicit `return` statements in Scala code. In Scala, the last expression in a method is automatically the return value, so explicit `return` is not idiomatic.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.RemoveRedundantToString
recipes.description: Removes calls to `.toString` on expressions that are already of type `String`. Such calls are redundant.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.RemoveUnitReturnType
recipes.description: Removes the explicit `Unit` return type annotation from Scala methods. In Scala, methods returning `Unit` do not need the `: Unit` annotation.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.RemoveUnusedBinding
recipes.description: Removes variable declarations whose name starts with `_` (underscore-prefixed binding). This removes unused variables that represent dead code.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.ResolveTodoComment
recipes.description: Finds comments containing TODO, FIXME, HACK, or XXX. These indicate incomplete work that should be tracked and resolved.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.ReviewDeprecatedApi
recipes.description: Finds declarations annotated with `@deprecated` in Scala code. Deprecated APIs should be reviewed for removal or migration.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.SimplifyBooleanExpression
recipes.description: Simplifies redundant boolean comparisons such as `x == true` to `x` and `x == false` to `!x`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.SimplifyOptionMatch
recipes.description: Rewrites `option match { case Some(x) => ...; case None => ... }` into the equivalent `map`, `flatMap`, or `getOrElse` combinator. Matches whose `None` branch yields `None` become `map` (when the `Some` branch wraps its result in `Some`) or `flatMap`; matches whose `Some` branch returns the bound value unchanged become `getOrElse`, which also covers a `None` branch that throws (its by-name argument keeps the throw lazy).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.UseCollectionConverters
recipes.description: `scala.collection.JavaConverters` was deprecated in Scala 2.13 in favor of `scala.jdk.CollectionConverters`. This recipe replaces the import automatically.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.UseDirectToSet
recipes.description: Replaces patterns like `.toList.toSet` or `.toSeq.toSet` with `.toSet` to avoid creating an unnecessary intermediate collection.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.UseLogger
recipes.description: Finds `println` calls in Scala code. Using `println` directly is not suitable for production; use a logging framework instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.UseLoggerForExceptions
recipes.description: Finds `.printStackTrace` calls. Use a logging framework instead of writing directly to `System.err`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.UseOptionSafely
recipes.description: Finds calls to `.get` on `Option` values. Calling `.get` on `Option` can throw `NoSuchElementException`; prefer `getOrElse`, `map`, `fold`, or pattern matching.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.cleanup.UseOrNull
recipes.description: Replaces `.getOrElse(null)` on `Option` values with `.orNull` for a cleaner, idiomatic alternative.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.concurrency.AvoidBlockingCalls
recipes.description: Finds `Await.result` and `Await.ready` calls which block the current thread. Consider using non-blocking Future composition with map, flatMap, or for-comprehensions.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.concurrency.AvoidThreadSleep
recipes.description: Finds `Thread.sleep` calls which block the current thread. Consider using scheduled executors or akka scheduler instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.concurrency.PreferCustomExecutionContext
recipes.description: Finds imports of `scala.concurrent.ExecutionContext.Implicits.global`. The global ExecutionContext may not be appropriate for blocking I/O operations; prefer a custom ExecutionContext backed by a dedicated thread pool.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.concurrency.SynchronizeMutableState
recipes.description: Finds `var` declarations at class level that lack `@volatile` or other synchronization annotations. Mutable shared state without synchronization is a common source of concurrency bugs.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.errorhandling.PreferDirectEitherOps
recipes.description: Finds usages of `.left` and `.right` projections on `Either`. Since Scala 2.13, `Either` is right-biased so `map`/`flatMap` work directly. Use `swap` to operate on the `Left` side instead of `.left`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.errorhandling.PreferFunctionalErrorHandling
recipes.displayName: Prefer functional error handling over `throw` expressions
recipes.description: Finds `throw` expressions inside method bodies that should use functional error handling. Throwing exceptions breaks referential transparency; prefer returning `Try`, `Either`, or `Option`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.errorhandling.UseNonFatalMatcher
recipes.displayName: Use `NonFatal` matcher for broad catch patterns
recipes.description: Finds catch blocks using broad patterns like `case e: Exception =>` or `case _ =>` that should use `scala.util.control.NonFatal` to catch all non-fatal exceptions while allowing fatal errors to propagate.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.errorhandling.UseTrySafely
recipes.description: Finds calls to `.get` on `scala.util.Try` values that should use safer alternatives. Calling `.get` on a `Failure` throws the contained exception; prefer `getOrElse`, `map`, or pattern matching.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.akka.MigrateActorRefTell
recipes.displayName: Migrate classic actor tell to typed ActorRef
recipes.description: Finds classic Akka actor messaging patterns (`actorRef ! msg` or `actorRef.tell(msg)`). Consider migrating to typed `ActorRef` messaging.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.akka.MigrateToTypedActor
recipes.displayName: Migrate classic Actor to Akka Typed Behavior
recipes.description: Removes `akka.actor.Actor` imports and marks classes extending `Actor` or `UntypedActor` from classic Akka for migration to Akka Typed `Behavior`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.akka.MigrateToTypedActorSystem
recipes.description: Replaces the import `akka.actor.ActorSystem` with `akka.actor.typed.ActorSystem` to migrate from the classic untyped actor system to Akka Typed.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.akka.RemoveDeprecatedAkkaImports
recipes.description: Removes imports of deprecated Akka APIs such as `akka.pattern.ask` (old ask pattern) and `akka.actor.PoisonPill`. These have no direct drop-in replacement and should be replaced with their modern Akka Typed equivalents.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.database.MigrateAnorm
recipes.displayName: Migrate Anorm to Doobie, Quill, or Skunk
recipes.description: Removes imports of the Anorm SQL library (`anorm.*`). Consider evaluating modern alternatives such as Doobie, Quill, or Skunk.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.database.MigratePhantomDsl
recipes.displayName: Migrate Phantom DSL to Datastax driver or quill-cassandra
recipes.description: Removes imports of the Phantom DSL library (`com.outworkers.phantom.*`). Consider migrating to the direct Datastax driver or quill-cassandra.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.database.MigrateScalikeJdbc
recipes.displayName: Migrate ScalikeJDBC to Doobie or Quill
recipes.description: Removes imports of the ScalikeJDBC library (`scalikejdbc.*`). Consider evaluating modern alternatives such as Doobie or Quill.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.database.SecureSqlQueries
recipes.description: Finds raw SQL string patterns such as `sql"..."`, `SQL(...)`, or `s"SELECT..."`. Ensure parameterized queries are used to prevent SQL injection.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.ecosystem.AvoidBlockingSlick
recipes.description: Finds methods that combine `Await.result` with `db.run`, indicating a blocking Slick database call. Use streaming or async patterns instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.ecosystem.MigrateCatsEffect2To3
recipes.displayName: Migrate Cats Effect 2 to Cats Effect 3
recipes.description: Finds Cats Effect 2 imports by detecting `cats.effect.IO` without `cats.effect.unsafe`, or CE2-specific types like `ContextShift` and `Timer`. Consider migrating to Cats Effect 3.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.ecosystem.MigrateScalazToCats
recipes.description: Removes imports of `scalaz.` packages. Scalaz is a legacy FP library; consider migrating to Cats or ZIO.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.ecosystem.UseCirceDerivation
recipes.description: Finds imports of `io.circe.generic.auto` which uses Shapeless-based automatic derivation. In Scala 3, consider using `derives` syntax for codec derivation instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.http.MigrateAkkaHttpToPekko
recipes.displayName: Find Akka HTTP imports to migrate to Apache Pekko
recipes.description: Finds imports starting with `akka.http`. Akka HTTP should be migrated to Apache Pekko HTTP (`org.apache.pekko.http`), the community-maintained fork.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.http.MigrateDispatch
recipes.displayName: Migrate Dispatch to sttp or http4s-client
recipes.description: Removes imports starting with `dispatch.`. Dispatch is an unmaintained HTTP client library; consider using sttp, http4s-client, or requests-scala.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.http.MigrateFinagle
recipes.displayName: Migrate Finagle to http4s, tapir, or pekko-http
recipes.description: Removes imports starting with `com.twitter.finagle`. Finagle is a legacy RPC framework; consider evaluating http4s, tapir, or pekko-http as alternatives.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.http.MigrateScalatra
recipes.displayName: Migrate Scalatra to http4s, tapir, or Play
recipes.description: Removes imports starting with `org.scalatra`. Scalatra is a servlet-based framework with declining activity; consider migrating to http4s, tapir, or Play Framework.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.json.MigrateJacksonScala
recipes.description: Removes imports of the Jackson Scala module (`com.fasterxml.jackson.module.scala.*`). Jackson is a Java-centric library and its Scala module can cause issues with Scala types. Consider using a Scala-native JSON library such as circe or zio-json. Removing the imports causes the compiler to highlight all usage sites that need updating.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.json.MigrateJson4s
recipes.description: Removes imports of the json4s library (`org.json4s.*`). json4s has known performance and maintenance concerns and should be replaced with a modern Scala JSON library such as circe or zio-json. Removing the imports causes the compiler to highlight all usage sites that need updating.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.json.MigrateLiftJson
recipes.description: Removes imports of the lift-json library (`net.liftweb.json.*`). lift-json is tightly coupled to the Lift framework and should be replaced with a standalone Scala JSON library such as circe or play-json. Removing the imports causes the compiler to highlight all usage sites that need updating.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.json.MigrateSprayJson
recipes.description: Removes imports of the spray-json library (`spray.json.*`). spray-json is no longer actively maintained and should be replaced with a modern Scala JSON library such as circe, play-json, or zio-json. Removing the imports causes the compiler to highlight all usage sites that need updating.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.MigrateImplicitToGivenUsing
recipes.description: Finds `implicit` keyword usage on methods and parameters. In Scala 3, `implicit` is replaced with `given`/`using`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.MigrateProcedureSyntax
recipes.description: Finds method declarations that use deprecated Scala procedure syntax (methods with a body block but no explicit return type or `=` sign). Procedure syntax was deprecated in Scala 2.13 and removed in Scala 3.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.play.InjectWsClient
recipes.description: Finds imports of the deprecated `play.api.libs.ws.WS` object. In Play 2.6+, `WS` was deprecated; inject `WSClient` instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.play.MigratePlayGlobalSettings
recipes.description: Finds classes extending `GlobalSettings` and imports of `play.api.GlobalSettings`. GlobalSettings is deprecated in Play 2.6+; use dependency injection instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.play.UseAsyncPlayAction
recipes.description: Finds Play controller actions (`Action {` or `Action.async {`) that contain `Await.result` blocking calls. Blocking inside Play Actions can exhaust the thread pool; use `Action.async` with `Future` instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.play.UsePlayJsonDirectly
recipes.description: Finds imports of `play.api.libs.json.Json` and usages of `Json.parse` or `Json.toJson` that may rely on deprecated implicit conversions. Consider using `play.api.libs.json.JsValue` directly.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.RemoveAny2StringAdd
recipes.description: Finds expressions like `1 + "string"` that rely on the deprecated `any2stringadd` implicit conversion. This was deprecated in Scala 2.13 and removed in Scala 3. Use string interpolation or `.toString` instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.RemoveExistentialTypes
recipes.description: Finds existential types using `forSome` syntax. Existential types were removed in Scala 3 and must be rewritten.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.RemoveSymbolLiterals
recipes.description: Finds symbol literals like `'foo` which were deprecated in Scala 2.13 and removed in Scala 3. Use `Symbol("foo")` instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.ReviewAbstractOverride
recipes.description: Finds methods or fields with both `abstract` and `override` modifiers. The stackable trait pattern using `abstract override` may need review for Scala 3.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.ReviewTraitVarInit
recipes.displayName: Review trait var initialization for Scala 3
recipes.description: Finds traits that have initialized `var` fields. In Scala 3, trait initialization semantics changed and these may need review.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.scala3.MigrateDelayedInit
recipes.description: Finds classes or objects extending `DelayedInit` or `App`. The `DelayedInit` trait was deprecated in Scala 2.13 and removed in Scala 3. Use `@main` annotation instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.scala3.MigrateXmlLiterals
recipes.displayName: Migrate XML literals to scala-xml interpolation
recipes.description: Finds XML literal usage in Scala code. XML literals were removed in Scala 3; use scala-xml library string interpolation instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.scala3.RemoveAutoTupling
recipes.description: Finds imports of `scala.language.autoTupling`. Auto-tupling is not available in Scala 3 and code relying on it must be rewritten.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.scala3.ReplaceDoWhileLoop
recipes.description: Finds `do-while` loops which were removed in Scala 3. Rewrite using a `while` loop with initial execution of the loop body.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.UpgradeSbtVersion
recipes.description: Update the `sbt.version` property in `project/build.properties` to the specified version. Only modifies files at `**/project/build.properties`.

options.name: version
options.description: The version to set for `sbt.version` in `project/build.properties`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.migrate.UseQuestionMarkWildcard
recipes.displayName: Use `?` instead of `_` for wildcard types (Scala 3)
recipes.description: Finds usage of `_` as a wildcard type in type parameters (e.g., `List[_]`). In Scala 3, the wildcard type syntax changed from `_` to `?`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.performance.PreferVectorOrPrepend
recipes.displayName: Prefer Vector or prepend for append-heavy workloads
recipes.description: Finds usage of the `:+` operator to append to a List, which is O(n). Prefer Vector for append-heavy workloads or prepend with `::` instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.performance.PreferViewMapValues
recipes.description: Finds calls to `.mapValues` which is deprecated in Scala 2.13+ and returns a lazy view instead of a strict Map. Use `.view.mapValues(...).toMap` instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.performance.UseCount
recipes.description: Replaces `.filter(f).size` or `.filter(f).length` chains with `.count(f)` to avoid creating an unnecessary intermediate collection.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.performance.UseFlatMap
recipes.description: Replaces `.map(f).flatten` chains with `.flatMap(f)` for clarity and to avoid creating an unnecessary intermediate collection.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.performance.UseHeadOption
recipes.description: Replaces `.head` calls on collections with `.headOption` to avoid `NoSuchElementException` on empty collections.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.performance.UseIsEmpty
recipes.description: Replaces `collection.size == 0` with `collection.isEmpty` for clarity and potential performance benefits.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.performance.UseLastOption
recipes.description: Replaces `.last` calls on collections with `.lastOption` to avoid `NoSuchElementException` on empty collections.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.performance.UseNonEmpty
recipes.description: Replaces `collection.size > 0` with `collection.nonEmpty` for clarity and potential performance benefits.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.safety.AvoidThrowInFinally
recipes.description: Finds `throw` statements inside `finally` blocks. Throwing in a `finally` block can mask the original exception, making debugging harder.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.safety.NarrowCatchClause
recipes.description: Finds catch blocks that catch `Throwable` and should be narrowed to specific exception types. Catching `Throwable` also catches fatal errors like `OutOfMemoryError` and `StackOverflowError`. Prefer catching specific exception types.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.safety.PreferConcurrentUtils
recipes.description: Finds `synchronized` blocks in Scala code. Consider using `java.util.concurrent` alternatives for better performance and composability.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.safety.RemoveUnusedImport
recipes.description: Removes imports where the imported simple name does not appear in the rest of the file. This is an approximate heuristic and may produce false positives.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.testing.MigrateSpecs2
recipes.displayName: Migrate specs2 to ScalaTest or MUnit
recipes.description: Finds imports of `org.specs2`. Consider migrating to ScalaTest or MUnit.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.testing.MigrateToAnyFlatSpec
recipes.description: Renames `FlatSpec` to `AnyFlatSpec` in extends clauses and updates the import from `org.scalatest.FlatSpec` to `org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec` (ScalaTest 3.x).

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.testing.UseNewScalaTestMatchers
recipes.description: Replaces imports of `org.scalatest.Matchers` or `org.scalatest.ShouldMatchers` with `org.scalatest.matchers.should.Matchers`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.scala.recipes.testing.UseScalaTestMatchers
recipes.displayName: Use ScalaTest matchers instead of `assert(x == y)`
recipes.description: Finds `assert(x == y)` patterns and `assertEquals` calls. Consider using ScalaTest matchers: `x shouldBe y`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.search.FindBuildMetadata
recipes.description: Find source files with matching build metadata.

options.name: key
options.description: The key to search for in the build metadata.

options.name: value
options.description: The value to search for in the build metadata.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.search.FindCommitters
recipes.description: List the committers on a repository.

options.name: fromDate
options.description: Optional. Take into account only commits since this date (inclusive). Default will be the entire history.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.search.FindParseToPrintInequality
recipes.description: OpenRewrite `Parser` implementations should produce `SourceFile` objects whose `printAll()` method should be byte-for-byte equivalent with the original source file. When this isn't true, recipes can still run on the `SourceFile` and even produce diffs, but the diffs would fail to apply as a patch to the original source file. Most `Parser` use `Parser#requirePrintEqualsInput` to produce a `ParseError` when they fail to produce a `SourceFile` that is print idempotent.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.search.RepositoryContainsFile
recipes.description: Intended to be used primarily as a precondition for other recipes, this recipe checks if a repository contains a specific file or files matching a pattern. If present all files in the repository are marked with a `SearchResult` marker. If you want to get only the matching file as a search result, use `FindSourceFiles` instead.

options.name: filePattern
options.description: A glob expression representing a file path to search for (relative to the project root). Blank/null matches all.Multiple patterns may be specified, separated by a semicolon `;`. If multiple patterns are supplied any of the patterns matching will be interpreted as a match.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.SetFilePermissions
recipes.description: Set a file's read, write and executable permission attributes.

options.name: fileMatcher
options.description: Permissions will be applied to matching files. This is a glob expression.

options.name: isReadable
options.description: File read permission.

options.name: isWritable
options.description: File write permission.

options.name: isExecutable
options.description: Files executable permission.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.Singleton
org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindCartesianJoin
recipes.description: Joins that lack a real linking predicate multiply row counts instead of matching related rows: an `ON` condition comparing a column to itself is always true, and comma-separated tables with no `WHERE` predicate relating them pair every row with every row. Explicit `CROSS JOIN` and `NATURAL` joins are treated as intentional and are not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindConstantPredicate
recipes.displayName: Find constant predicates that are always true or always false
recipes.description: A comparison whose operands are both constant, such as `1 = 1` or `1 = 0`, evaluates the same for every row regardless of the data. Combined with `OR` an always-true constant makes the whole condition always true, so every row matches and the other filters are ignored; an always-false constant used as a filter can never be satisfied, so the query returns nothing. An always-true constant on its own or joined with `AND`, a common query-builder idiom, is not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindCorrelatedAggregateSubquery
recipes.description: A scalar subquery that computes an aggregate like `MAX` while referencing the outer query runs once per outer row on engines that cannot decorrelate it. A window function or a join to a pre-aggregated derived table computes every group in a single pass. Uncorrelated aggregate subqueries and `EXISTS` or `IN` subqueries are not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindCountAsExistenceCheck
recipes.displayName: Find `COUNT` subqueries used as existence checks
recipes.description: A scalar `COUNT` subquery compared to `0` or `1` tallies every matching row even though the outcome is decided by the first one. `EXISTS` or `NOT EXISTS` lets the engine stop as soon as a match is found. Comparisons against other values, such as `> 5`, express a genuine cardinality requirement and are not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindDistinctWithJoin
recipes.description: `DISTINCT` paired with a `JOIN` frequently compensates for row multiplication that a correct join condition or an `EXISTS` test would avoid, and `DISTINCT` alongside `GROUP BY` is redundant because grouping already collapses duplicate rows. A `DISTINCT` on a single-table query without `GROUP BY` is not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindDmlWithoutWhere
recipes.displayName: Find `UPDATE` and `DELETE` statements without a `WHERE` clause
recipes.description: An `UPDATE` or `DELETE` with no `WHERE` clause touches every row in the table, holding locks for the duration, flooding replication, and risking unintended data loss if the missing predicate was an oversight.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindHavingWithoutAggregate
recipes.displayName: Find `HAVING` conditions that use no aggregate
recipes.description: A `HAVING` condition that references no aggregate forces the database to build every group before throwing unwanted ones away. The same condition in `WHERE` filters rows before grouping, doing strictly less work.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindInsertWithoutColumns
recipes.displayName: Find `INSERT ... VALUES` statements that omit the column list
recipes.description: An `INSERT ... VALUES` with no column list binds each value to a column by position, so adding, dropping, or reordering a column silently shifts values into the wrong columns or breaks the statement; naming the target columns keeps it correct across schema changes. `INSERT ... SELECT` is left alone, since its projection makes the column correspondence explicit.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindLeadingWildcardLike
recipes.displayName: Find `LIKE` patterns starting with a wildcard
recipes.description: A `LIKE` pattern whose first character is `%` or `_` gives the database no prefix to seek in a B-tree index, so every row must be inspected. When a prefix search is not possible, a trigram or full-text index can serve the query instead. Parameter placeholders and patterns with only trailing wildcards are not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindLimitWithoutOrderBy
recipes.displayName: Find row limiters without an `ORDER BY`
recipes.description: A `LIMIT`, `OFFSET`, `FETCH`, or `TOP` clause selects a subset of rows, but without an `ORDER BY` the engine is free to return any rows in any order, so the result is arbitrary and can differ from one execution to the next. Queries that can only ever produce a single row, such as a bare aggregate with no `GROUP BY`, and limiters inside an `EXISTS` subquery, where order does not matter, are not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindNonSargablePredicate
recipes.description: A comparison that wraps a column in a function, `CAST`, or arithmetic must evaluate the expression for every row, so an index on the bare column cannot be used for a range scan. Keeping the column alone on one side, e.g. `amount > 100 - 1` rather than `amount + 1 > 100`, keeps the predicate index-eligible.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindNotInSubquery
recipes.description: When the subquery can return a `NULL`, `NOT IN` evaluates to unknown for every row and the outer query silently returns nothing. Many planners also fail to rewrite `NOT IN` as an efficient anti-join. `NOT EXISTS` avoids both problems. `NOT IN` over a literal list is not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindOffsetPagination
recipes.description: `OFFSET n` reads and throws away `n` rows before returning any, so each later page costs linearly more than the one before it. Parameterized offsets and large literal offsets are flagged; keyset pagination (`WHERE key > last-seen ORDER BY key`) reads only the requested page. Small literal offsets are not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindOptionalParameterOr
recipes.displayName: Find optional filters written as `OR` parameter `IS NULL`
recipes.description: The `col = ? OR ? IS NULL` pattern turns a filter on and off at runtime, so the planner must settle on one generic plan that works for every parameter combination instead of an index-driven plan for the filtered case. An `IS NULL` test on a column inside an `OR` is ordinary SQL and is not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindOrderByRandom
recipes.displayName: Find `ORDER BY` on a random function
recipes.description: Sorting by `RAND()`, `RANDOM()`, `NEWID()`, or `DBMS_RANDOM` computes a random value for every row and sorts the entire table just to keep a few rows. Sample by a key range or use the dialect's table sampling instead.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindOversizedInList
recipes.description: A very long `IN` list is parsed and planned on every execution, tends to pollute the statement cache, and some databases hard-cap the number of elements it may contain. Loading the values into a temporary table and joining against it scales far better. `IN` with a subquery is not flagged.

options.name: threshold
options.description: Flag `IN` lists with more values than this. Defaults to 50 when not set.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindScalarSubqueryInSelect
recipes.displayName: Find scalar subqueries in the `SELECT` list
recipes.description: A subquery used as an expression in the `SELECT` list may execute once per result row, turning a single scan into N+1 queries. A `JOIN` (or `LATERAL` join) produces the same values in one pass. Subqueries in `WHERE`, `FROM`, or `JOIN` conditions are not flagged.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindSelectStar
recipes.description: Wildcard projections fetch columns the code does not use, defeat covering indexes, and change behavior when the schema changes. `SELECT *` under `EXISTS (...)` or inside aggregate functions like `COUNT(*)` is not flagged because no columns are materialized there.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.FindUnionInsteadOfUnionAll
recipes.description: Plain `UNION` de-duplicates the combined rows, forcing a sort or hash over the entire result even when the branches cannot overlap. `UNION ALL` skips that work. `UNION` inside a `WITH` item is not flagged because recursive CTEs rely on plain `UNION` semantics to terminate.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.RemoveOrderByInSubquery
recipes.description: An `ORDER BY` inside a subquery or CTE without a `LIMIT`, `OFFSET`, or `FETCH` does not affect the rows the outer query returns, so the database either discards the sort or pays for ordering that nothing observes. Remove the clause, leaving the rest of the statement untouched. Sort in the outermost query if a specific order is required.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.ReplaceNullComparisonWithIsNull
recipes.displayName: Replace `= NULL` and `<> NULL` with `IS NULL` and `IS NOT NULL`
recipes.description: Under three-valued logic a comparison with `NULL` evaluates to UNKNOWN rather than true, so `col = NULL` and `col <> NULL` match no rows. Rewrite them to the intended `col IS NULL` and `col IS NOT NULL`, changing only the compared operator so the rest of the statement is left untouched.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.antipattern.SqlAntiPatterns
recipes.displayName: Find and fix SQL performance anti-patterns
recipes.description: Analyzes SQL found in code and resource files for statically detectable performance anti-patterns such as `SELECT *`, `COUNT(*)` used as an existence check, scalar subqueries in the `SELECT` list, non-sargable predicates, and missing join conditions. Every occurrence is reported to the `SqlAntiPatterns` data table with a severity and suggested remediation, then fixed in place where a safe rewrite exists or marked in source otherwise.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.sql.ChangeFunctionName
recipes.description: When migrating between dialects, often one name can be substituted for another. For example, Oracle's `NVL` function can be replaced with Postgres `COALESCE`.

options.name: oldFunctionName
options.description: The name of the function to find, case insensitive.

options.name: newFunctionName

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.AbstractClassPublicConstructor
recipes.displayName: Constructors of an `abstract` class should not be declared `public`
recipes.description: Constructors of `abstract` classes can only be called in constructors of their subclasses. Therefore the visibility of `public` constructors are reduced to `protected`. Declaring them `public` is misleading since it implies they could be invoked directly, which is never possible.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.AddSerialAnnotationToSerialVersionUID
recipes.description: Annotate any `serialVersionUID` fields with `@Serial` to indicate it's part of the serialization mechanism.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.AddSerialVersionUidToSerializable
recipes.displayName: Add `serialVersionUID` to a `Serializable` class when missing
recipes.description: A `serialVersionUID` field is strongly recommended in all `Serializable` classes. If this is not defined on a `Serializable` class, the compiler will generate this value. If a change is later made to the class, the generated value will change and attempts to deserialize the class will fail. Explicitly declaring this field gives you control over binary compatibility across versions.

options.name: uid
options.description: Value of the added serial version UID.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.AllBranchesIdentical
recipes.displayName: All branches in a conditional should not have the same implementation
recipes.description: When every branch of an `if`/`else` chain executes the same code, the condition serves no purpose and the code block can be used directly.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.AnnotateNullableMethods
recipes.displayName: Annotate methods which may return `null` with `@Nullable`
recipes.description: Add `@Nullable` to non-private methods that may return `null`. By default `org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable` is used, but through the `nullableAnnotationClass` option a custom annotation can be provided. Both `@Target(TYPE_USE)` and declaration annotations (e.g. `javax.annotation.CheckForNull`) are supported. Methods that already carry a known nullable annotation (matched by simple name) are skipped to avoid duplication. This recipe scans for methods that do not already have a `@Nullable` annotation and checks their return statements for potential null values. It also identifies known methods from standard libraries that may return null, such as methods from `Map`, `Queue`, `Deque`, `NavigableSet`, and `Spliterator`. The return of streams, or lambdas are not taken into account.

options.name: nullableAnnotationClass
options.description: The fully qualified name of the @Nullable annotation to add. Both `@Target(TYPE_USE)` and declaration annotations (e.g. `javax.annotation.CheckForNull`) are supported. Defaults to `org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.AnnotateNullableParameters
recipes.description: Add `@Nullable` to parameters of public methods that are explicitly checked for `null`. By default `org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable` is used, but through the `nullableAnnotationClass` option a custom annotation can be provided. Both `@Target(TYPE_USE)` and declaration annotations (e.g. `javax.annotation.CheckForNull`) are supported. Parameters that already carry a known nullable annotation are skipped to avoid duplication. This recipe scans for methods that do not already have parameters annotated with a nullable annotation and checks their usages for potential null checks. Additional null-checking methods can be specified via the `additionalNullCheckingMethods` option.

options.name: nullableAnnotationClass
options.description: The fully qualified name of the @Nullable annotation to add. Both `@Target(TYPE_USE)` and declaration annotations (e.g. `javax.annotation.CheckForNull`) are supported. Defaults to `org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable`.

options.name: additionalNullCheckingMethods
options.description: A list of method patterns (in OpenRewrite MethodMatcher format) that should be considered as null-checking methods. These will be added to the built-in list of known null-checking methods. Use `..` for any parameters, e.g., `com.mycompany.utils.StringUtil isEmpty(..)` or `com.mycompany.utils.CollectionUtil isNullOrEmpty(java.util.Collection)`

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.AnnotateRequiredParameters
recipes.description: Add `@NonNull` to parameters of public methods that are explicitly checked for `null` and throw an exception if null. By default `org.jspecify.annotations.NonNull` is used, but through the `nonNullAnnotationClass` option a custom annotation can be provided. When providing a custom `nonNullAnnotationClass` that annotation should be meta annotated with `@Target(TYPE_USE)`. This recipe scans for methods that do not already have parameters annotated with `@NonNull` annotation and checks for null validation patterns that throw exceptions, such as `if (param == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException()`.

options.name: nonNullAnnotationClass
options.description: The fully qualified name of the @NonNull annotation. The annotation should be meta annotated with `@Target(TYPE_USE)`. Defaults to `org.jspecify.annotations.NonNull`

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.AtomicPrimitiveEqualsUsesGet
recipes.displayName: Atomic Boolean, Integer, and Long equality checks compare their values
recipes.description: `AtomicBoolean#equals(Object)`, `AtomicInteger#equals(Object)` and `AtomicLong#equals(Object)` are only equal to their instance. This recipe converts `a.equals(b)` to `a.get() == b.get()`. These atomic classes do not override `equals` from `Object`, so calling it compares object identity rather than the wrapped value, which is almost never the intended behavior.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.AvoidBoxedBooleanExpressions
recipes.description: Under certain conditions the `java.lang.Boolean` type is used as an expression, and it may throw a `NullPointerException` if the value is null. Using `Boolean.TRUE.equals(...)` guards against unboxing a `null` reference in control flow positions like `if` conditions and ternary operators.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.BigDecimalDoubleConstructorRecipe
recipes.description:
Use of `new BigDecimal(double)` constructor can lead to loss of precision. Use `BigDecimal.valueOf(double)` instead.
For example writing `new BigDecimal(0.1)` does not create a `BigDecimal` which is exactly equal to `0.1`, but it is equal to `0.1000000000000000055511151231257827021181583404541015625`. This is because `0.1` cannot be represented exactly as a double (or, for that matter, as a binary fraction of any finite length). `BigDecimal.valueOf` avoids this by converting through a string representation, preserving the value you actually intended.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.BigDecimalRoundingConstantsToEnums
recipes.description: Convert `BigDecimal` rounding constants to the equivalent `RoundingMode` enum. The integer-based rounding constants on `BigDecimal` are deprecated and lack type safety; the `RoundingMode` enum makes the rounding behavior self-documenting and prevents invalid values.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.BooleanChecksNotInverted
recipes.displayName: Boolean checks should not be inverted
recipes.description: Ensures that boolean checks are not unnecessarily inverted. Also fixes double negative boolean expressions. Negating a comparison and then inverting it adds cognitive overhead; using the direct operator (e.g., `>=` instead of `!(... < ...)`) is clearer and easier to reason about.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.BufferedWriterCreationRecipes
recipes.displayName: Modernize `BufferedWriter` creation & prevent file descriptor leaks
recipes.description: The code `new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(f))` creates a `BufferedWriter` that does not close the underlying `FileWriter` when it is closed. This can lead to file descriptor leaks as per [CWE-755](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/755.html). Use `Files.newBufferedWriter` to create a `BufferedWriter` that closes the underlying file descriptor when it is closed.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.BufferedWriterCreationRecipes$BufferedWriterFromNewFileWriterWithFileAndBooleanArgumentsRecipe
recipeList.displayName: Convert `new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(File, boolean))` to `Files.newBufferedWriter(Path, StandardOpenOption)`

recipes.description: Convert `new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(f, b))` to `Files.newBufferedWriter(f.toPath(), b ? StandardOpenOption.APPEND : StandardOpenOption.CREATE)`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.BufferedWriterCreationRecipes$BufferedWriterFromNewFileWriterWithFileArgumentRecipe
recipes.description: Convert `new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(f))` to `Files.newBufferedWriter(f.toPath())`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.BufferedWriterCreationRecipes$BufferedWriterFromNewFileWriterWithStringAndBooleanArgumentsRecipe
recipes.displayName: Convert `new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(String, boolean))` to `Files.newBufferedWriter(Path, StandardOpenOption)`
recipes.description: Convert `new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(s, b))` to `Files.newBufferedWriter(new java.io.File(s).toPath(), b ? StandardOpenOption.APPEND : StandardOpenOption.CREATE)`.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.CaseInsensitiveComparisonsDoNotChangeCase
recipes.displayName: CaseInsensitive comparisons do not alter case
recipes.description: Remove `String#toLowerCase()` or `String#toUpperCase()` from `String#equalsIgnoreCase(..)` comparisons. Changing case before a case-insensitive comparison is redundant and allocates unnecessary intermediate `String` objects.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.CatchClauseOnlyRethrows
recipes.displayName: Catch clause should do more than just rethrow
recipes.description: A `catch` clause that only rethrows the caught exception is unnecessary. Letting the exception bubble up as normal achieves the same result with less code. Such catch blocks add visual noise and indentation without changing program behavior.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.ChainStringBuilderAppendCalls
recipes.description: String concatenation within calls to `StringBuilder.append()` causes unnecessary memory allocation. Except for concatenations of String literals, which are joined together at compile time. Replaces inefficient concatenations with chained calls to `StringBuilder.append()`. Using `+` inside `append()` defeats the purpose of the `StringBuilder`, since the concatenation creates a temporary `String` before appending.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.CodeCleanup
recipes.description: Automatically cleanup code, e.g. remove unnecessary parentheses, simplify expressions.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.java.format.EmptyNewlineAtEndOfFile
recipeList.displayName: End files with a single newline

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.ForLoopControlVariablePostfixOperators
recipeList.displayName: `for` loop counters should use postfix operators

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.RemoveMethodsOnlyCallSuper
recipeList.displayName: Remove methods that only call super

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.java.ShortenFullyQualifiedTypeReferences
recipeList.displayName: Add imports for fully qualified references to types

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.CollapsibleIfStatements
recipes.description: When an `if` statement body contains only another `if` with no `else`, the two conditions can be combined with `&&`. Merging the conditions reduces nesting and makes the code easier to read.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.CollectionToArrayShouldHaveProperType
recipes.displayName: 'Collection.toArray()' should be passed an array of the proper type
recipes.description: Using `Collection.toArray()` without parameters returns an `Object[]`, which requires casting. It is more efficient and clearer to use `Collection.toArray(new T[0])` instead. The parameterless form can cause a `ClassCastException` at runtime when the returned `Object[]` is cast to a more specific array type.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.CombineSemanticallyEqualCatchBlocks
recipes.description: Combine catches in a try that contain semantically equivalent blocks. No change will be made when a caught exception exists if combining catches may change application behavior or type attribution is missing. Merging duplicate catch bodies into multi-catch blocks reduces repetition and makes the exception handling strategy easier to follow.

recipes.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.CommonDeclarationSiteTypeVariances
recipes.displayName: Properly use declaration-site type variance for well-known types
recipes.description: When using a method parameter like `Function<IN, OUT>`, it should rather be `Function<? super IN, ? extends OUT>`. This recipe checks for method parameters of well-known types.

recipeList.name: org.openrewrite.staticanalysis.RemoveRedundantNullCheckBeforeLiteralEquals
